definition_zh: 必须；一定；必需品
definition_en: used to say that something is necessary or almost certainly true; as a noun, something that cannot be left out
core_image: 一道关着的闸门，旁边只留一条必须走过去的通道
scene: 地铁入口处，安检员抬手示意乘客停下，把背包放上检查带。You must put your bag on the belt before you walk through.
sceneCN: 这里是「必须、有义务」（第 1 个义项：被要求做某事）；句意为过闸之前你得出示并放下背包接受检查。图中可辨识物件：闸门、检查带、背包。

collocations.zh: 一定做过（对过去的推测）

derivatives.zh: 由 must 与 have 复合，义为「必备品」
由 must 与 see 复合，义为「必看之物」

senses.title: To be obliged to do something
senses.definition: used to say that a person is obliged or forced to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人有义务或不得不做某事
senses.example: You must show your ticket at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须在门口出示车票。
senses.why: Old English moste was the past of motan and often meant had to; the old sense of permission narrowed into a demand, so the word now states an obligation rather than an option.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 moste 是 motan 的过去式，常表示「当时不得不」；原先的许可义收窄成强制义，所以这个词现在陈述的是义务，而不是选项。

senses.title: To be very likely true
senses.definition: used to say that something is almost certainly true, judging from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 依据证据判断某事几乎肯定成立
senses.example: The lights are off; they must have gone home.
senses.exampleCN: 灯都灭了，他们一定已经回家了。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be avoided, the mind treats the conclusion as unavoidable too, so the force of obligation slides into inference about what has to be the case.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事无法回避，人心也会把相应结论看成躲不开的，于是义务的力量滑向「情况必然如此」的推断。

senses.title: Something that cannot be left out
senses.definition: a thing that is absolutely necessary or strongly recommended
senses.definitionCN: 绝对必要或强烈建议不可省略的事物
senses.example: A torch is a must when you camp in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 在山里露营，手电是必备的。
senses.why: The noun keeps the force of the modal: anything called a must is treated as something one cannot skip, which is how a demand turns into an object on a packing list.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法保留了情态动词的力量：被称作 a must 的东西，被当成不能跳过的事物，于是一项要求就变成了清单上的一个物件。

intro.en: Must grew out of an Old English verb for being able or allowed; its past tense took over the present meaning of obligation.
intro.cn: must 源自古英语中表示「能够、被允许」的动词，它的过去式后来接管了现在时的义务义。

items.en: The verb reconstructed as motan is generally thought to have meant to have room or power to do something.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 motan 意为「有做某事的余地或力量」。

items.en: Motan meant to be able or to be permitted, and its past tense moste often carried the practical sense of having to.
items.cn: motan 意为能够或被允许，其过去式 moste 常带有「只好、不得不」的实感。

items.en: Moste spread into more contexts than the old present form, and speakers began to use it for present obligations.
items.cn: moste 的使用范围超过了旧的现在式，说话人开始用它表达当下的义务。

items.en: Must settled as an unchanging present form, took a contracted negative mustn't, and lost the old infinitive and participle.
items.cn: must 固定为没有词形变化的现在式，出现缩略否定 mustn't，旧的动词不定式和分词形式逐渐消失。

items.en: Modern English adds the inference use and the countable noun a must, plus compounds such as must-have and must-see.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了推测用法和可数名词 a must，还产生 must-have、must-see 这类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the negative contraction and three words that only resemble must in spelling; the near-meaning group holds other ways of expressing obligation.
note.cn: 形近组收 must 的否定缩略式，以及三个只是拼写相似、来源不同的词；近义组收其他表示义务的说法。

entries.definition: The contracted negative of must, common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: must 的否定缩略形式，口语中常见。

entries.definition: To gather people or courage for a purpose; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 召集人员或鼓起勇气；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A yellow sharp condiment made from seeds; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 用种子制成的黄色辛辣调味酱；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Smelling damp and stale, as an old room does; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 有潮湿霉味的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Expresses external obligation like must, but uses do in questions and negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 与 must 一样表示外在义务，但疑问和否定要借助 do。

entries.definition: Gives advice or a mild duty rather than a firm demand.
entries.definitionCN: 给出建议或轻微责任，语气不如 must 强硬。

entries.definition: States a duty seen as right, often in careful or written English.
entries.definitionCN: 表示按道理应尽的责任，多见于正式或书面英语。

entries.definition: Names a requirement, usually followed by to before a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指出一项需求，动词前通常带 to。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic modal that drifted from permission to obligation, with a negative contraction and two modern compounds around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语情态动词，从许可漂移到义务，周围还有一个否定缩略式和两个现代复合词。

normal.en: Old English motan meant to be able or allowed, and its past moste meant had to; must is that past form grown into a present.
normal.cn: 古英语 motan 意为能够、被允许，其过去式 moste 意为不得不；must 就是这个过去式长成了现在式。

normal.en: Must is followed by the bare verb: must go, never must to go.
normal.cn: must 后面直接跟动词原形：说 must go，不说 must to go。

normal.en: Mustn't forbids, while can't denies a guess: you mustn't smoke here, but he can't be at home.
normal.cn: mustn't 表示禁止，can't 才用来否定推测：此处不许吸烟，而「他不可能在家」要用 can't。

normal.en: Must have done looks back at a past certainty, which is why the perfect follows must, not the past tense.
normal.cn: must have done 回看一件过去确定的事，所以 must 后面接完成式，而不是过去式。

normal.en: The noun a must copies the modal's force: a must-have item is one you cannot leave out.
normal.cn: 名词 a must 沿用了情态动词的力量：a must-have item 就是不能省略的东西。

abstract.en: A gate that only opens one way turns an old permission word into a word of compulsion.
abstract.cn: 一道只能单向打开的闸门，把旧的许可词变成了强制词。

abstract.en: When no other route exists, a demand and a certainty feel like the same pressure.
abstract.cn: 当没有别的路可走，一项要求和一种确定感会显得是同一种压力。

abstract.en: Every packing list is a small museum of things someone decided they could not do without.
abstract.cn: 每一张行李清单，都是「有人认定不能没有」的小小陈列馆。

examples.en: Visitors must sign in at the front desk.
examples.cn: 访客必须在前台登记。

examples.en: She must have missed the last bus.
examples.cn: 她一定是错过了末班车。

examples.en: A good pair of gloves is a must in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天一副好手套是必备的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马斯特」——教练马斯特站在跑道边说：必须跑完这一圈；must 就是必须。

root: 古英语 motan（能够、被允许），过去式 moste 逐渐固定为 must；一般认为与德语 müssen 同出原始日耳曼语 motan，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unavoidable demand; from it grow the inference about what must be true and the noun for a thing one cannot leave out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是躲不开的要求；由此长出「情况必然如此」的推断，以及指「不能省略之物」的名词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate with only one open passage, where stopping is not an option.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道只留一条通道的闸门，停下不在选项之内。

intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的一个情态动词、它的过去式、一个否定附着成分，以及两个把情态动词变成名词的现代复合词支撑。

latinIntro.cn: must 属于日耳曼语情态动词，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 相互的；彼此的；共同的（后一义常被批评为宽松用法）
definition_en: given, felt, or done by each side toward the other in exchange; also shared in common by two or more parties
core_image: 两只手同时递出同一把钥匙：你给我，我也给你
scene: 两位邻居隔着栅栏交换对方大门的钥匙，各替对方保管一把备用钥匙。Two neighbours stand at the fence and hand each other a key to the other's gate; their help is mutual, since each one keeps a spare key for the other.
sceneCN: 这里 mutual 是「互相给予、彼此交换」（第 1 个义项：两方对等地给出并接受）；句意：两位邻居站在篱笆边，各自把对方院门的钥匙递给对方，他们的帮助是相互的，因为各自都为对方留了一把备用钥匙。图中可辨识物件：木篱笆、两把钥匙、两只同时伸出的手、两扇院门；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Reciprocally given: both sides exchange
senses.titleCN: 互相给予：两边都在交换
senses.definition: given by each side to the other, so that what one gives is returned in kind
senses.definitionCN: 一方给出的，另一方也以同类回报；给予与接受同时发生在两边
senses.example: Their help was mutual: each repaired what the other had broken.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的帮助是相互的：各自修好了对方弄坏的东西。
senses.why: Late 15c. mutual was first used of feelings and meant 'reciprocally given and received'. The core picture is an exchange: I give, you give back.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪晚期 mutual 最先用于感情，义为“相互给予并接受”。核心画面是一次交换：我给，你也给回来。

senses.title: Mutual affection: a feeling each holds for the other
senses.titleCN: 相互的情感：各自对对方怀有同样的心
senses.definition: of a feeling, held by two people each toward the other, so that the regard is returned
senses.definitionCN: 指一种情感，两人各自对对方怀有，因而这份心意是被回应的
senses.example: The mutual affection between the two sisters lasted all their lives.
senses.exampleCN: 两姐妹之间的相互关爱持续了一生。
senses.why: A feeling can itself be the thing exchanged. Each heart holds the same regard, so the emotion is returned rather than held on one side only.
senses.whyCN: 情感本身就可以是被交换的东西。两颗心怀着同样的心意，因此这份情感是被回应的，而不是只停留在一边。

senses.title: The disputed mutual friend: a person known to both
senses.titleCN: 备受争议的 mutual friend：两人都认识的人
senses.definition: a person whom two other people both know, whether or not those two know each other through that person
senses.definitionCN: 两个人都认识的人，不论这两人是否正因此人而相识
senses.example: We met through a mutual friend at the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 我们经一位共同的朋友在博物馆相识。
senses.why: The 1630s 'common' sense let mutual describe what two parties share. Victorian critics attacked a mutual friend because a friend is not exchanged, yet the phrase is now standard.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 30 年代出现的“共同”义，让 mutual 可以形容两方共享之物。维多利亚时代的批评者攻击 a mutual friend，因为朋友并不是被“交换”的；但这一说法如今已属标准。

senses.title: Shared in common: a quality both possess
senses.titleCN: 共同拥有：两方都具有的性质
senses.definition: held or possessed in common by two or more parties, with no idea of exchange
senses.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同持有或拥有，不含交换之意
senses.example: Their mutual interest in birds began at the same observatory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对鸟类的共同兴趣始于同一座观测站。
senses.why: From the 1630s mutual widened from exchange to possession: two parties hold the same thing. This branch is the loose 'common' use that style guides still argue about.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 30 年代起，mutual 从“交换”扩展到“持有”：两方握着同一样东西。这条分支就是用法指南至今仍在争论的宽松“共同”义。

senses.title: Mutual benefit: advantage that runs both ways
senses.definition: producing advantage for each of the parties involved, so that neither gains at the other's expense
senses.definitionCN: 为涉及的每一方都带来好处，没有一方以另一方受损为代价获利
senses.example: The trade deal was based on mutual benefit rather than charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这项贸易协定建立在互利而非施舍之上。
senses.why: Benefit follows the exchange image: each side hands over something and receives something in return, so the gain travels in both directions.
senses.whyCN: benefit 延续了交换意象：每一方交出一些东西，又得到一些回报，因此好处是双向流动的。

senses.title: Mutual agreement: a promise binding both sides
senses.titleCN: 双方协议：约束两边的承诺
senses.definition: an arrangement accepted by both parties and binding each of them equally
senses.definitionCN: 两方都接受、并同等约束双方的安排
senses.example: They ended the lease by mutual agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们经双方同意终止了租约。
senses.why: An agreement is exchanged as promises: each gives a pledge and receives one. Because both are bound, the obligation is mutual in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: 协议是以承诺作交换：各方给出一份保证，也收到一份保证。由于双方都受约束，这种义务是严格意义上的“相互的”。

senses.title: Mutual insurance: a company owned by its members
senses.titleCN: 互助保险：由会员共同拥有的公司
senses.definition: of an insurer or society owned by its policyholders, who share the risks and the profits
senses.definitionCN: 指由保单持有人共同拥有的保险机构，成员分担风险、共享收益
senses.example: The mutual insurance society returned part of the premium to every member.
senses.exampleCN: 这家互助保险社把部分保费返还给每位成员。
senses.why: Members pay in and cover one another, so the exchange is pooled rather than one-to-one. Mutual names the arrangement in which each member is both payer and owner.
senses.whyCN: 成员缴钱并相互保障，交换因此被汇聚起来，而不是一对一进行。mutual 命名的是这样一种安排：每个成员既是付款人又是所有者。

senses.title: Mutual fund: money pooled and shared
senses.titleCN: 共同基金：汇集并共享的资金
senses.definition: a fund in which many investors pool money and share the returns, recorded from 1950
senses.definitionCN: 众多投资者汇集资金并共享收益的基金，该说法记录于 1950 年
senses.example: She put her savings into a mutual fund rather than a single stock.
senses.exampleCN: 她把积蓄投入共同基金，而不是单只股票。
senses.why: Here mutual marks a pool: every investor holds a share of the same whole. The exchange is between members and the fund, and the ownership is shared.
senses.whyCN: 这里 mutual 标记的是一口“资金池”：每位投资者都持有同一整体的份额。交换发生在成员与基金之间，所有权则是共享的。

senses.title: Mutual relation: each term implies the other
senses.titleCN: 相互关系：每一项都蕴含另一项
senses.definition: in logic and mathematics, of a relation in which each of two terms entails or points to the other
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑与数学中，指两项之间每一项都蕴含或指向另一项的关系
senses.example: In logic, entailment is mutual when each of two propositions follows from the other.
senses.exampleCN: 在逻辑中，当两个命题各自都能推出对方时，蕴含关系就是相互的。
senses.why: The exchange becomes formal: A gives support to B and B gives support back to A. Mutual relation names this perfect two-way dependency.
senses.whyCN: 交换在这里变得形式化：A 给 B 支撑，B 也给 A 支撑。mutual relation 命名的是这种完美的双向依赖。

senses.title: Mutual assured destruction: a guarantee aimed both ways
senses.titleCN: 相互确保摧毁：对准两边的保证
senses.definition: the Cold War doctrine that a full nuclear exchange would destroy both sides, so neither would strike first; abbreviated MAD in 1966
senses.definitionCN: 冷战理论：全面核交换将摧毁双方，因此谁都不敢先动手；1966 年缩写为 MAD
senses.example: Mutual assured destruction gave the Cold War its strangest acronym, MAD.
senses.exampleCN: 相互确保摧毁给冷战留下了最古怪的缩写 MAD。
senses.why: Each side guarantees the other's destruction, so the threat is returned in full. The word's exchange core hardens into a deadly symmetry.
senses.whyCN: 每一方都保证对方的毁灭，威胁被完整地回敬过去。这个词的“交换”核心在这里硬化成一种致命的对称。

intro.en: Mutual entered English in the late 15c. from Old French mutuel, and its first sense was an exchange of feeling, not joint ownership. The 'common' sense is a later and often criticised extension.
intro.cn: mutual 于 15 世纪晚期从古法语 mutuel 进入英语，最初的义项是情感的交换，而不是共同拥有。“共同”义是后来出现、且常受批评的扩展。

items.en: First recorded in the late 15c., used of feelings in the sense 'reciprocally given and received'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 15 世纪晚期，用于感情，义为“相互给予并接受”。

items.en: From Old French mutuel (14c.), which passed the Latin adjective into French.
items.cn: 来自古法语 mutuel（14 世纪），该词把拉丁语形容词带入了法语。

items.en: Latin mutuus meant 'reciprocal, done in exchange'; the stem mut- carries the idea of change and exchange.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus 意为“相互的、交换而成的”；词干 mut- 带有“改变、交换”的意思。

items.en: Traced to PIE *mei-(1) 'to change, go, move'. Watkins adds that its derivatives concern goods and services exchanged by custom or law.
items.cn: 可追溯至原始印欧语 *mei-(1)“改变、去、移动”。Watkins 补充说，该词根的衍生词与社会中按习俗或法律进行的货物与服务交换有关。

items.en: The sense 'common, shared' appears in the 1630s and was already noted as loosely misused, especially in a mutual friend.
items.cn: “共同的、共享的”义在 17 世纪 30 年代出现，当时就已被指出常被宽松误用，尤其见于 a mutual friend。

items.en: Mutual fund is recorded from 1950 and mutual assured destruction, or MAD, from 1966; both keep the two-way picture.
items.cn: mutual fund 记录于 1950 年，mutual assured destruction（缩写 MAD）记录于 1966 年；两者都保留了双向的画面。

note.en: The first group shares the mut- stem or sound, the second shares the meaning of two-way or shared, so form and sense stay apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享 mut- 词干或读音，第二组共享“双向／共享”的词义，这样词形与词义不会被混为一谈。

entries.definition: liable to change. It comes from Latin mutare 'to change', the same PIE family as mutuus, but means changeable rather than exchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 易变的。它来自拉丁语 mutare“改变”，与 mutuus 同属一个原始印欧语词族，但意思是“可变的”，不是“被交换的”。

entries.definition: a change of form or genetic material. It is built on mutare 'to change', not on mutuus 'reciprocal'.
entries.definitionCN: 形态改变；基因突变。它建立在 mutare“改变”上，而不是 mutuus“相互的”上。

entries.definition: to travel regularly to work, or to reduce a punishment. It comes from Latin commutare 'to exchange, change', com- plus mutare.
entries.definitionCN: 通勤；减刑。它来自拉丁语 commutare“交换、改变”，由 com- 加 mutare 构成。

entries.definition: given or done by each side to the other. It is the strict term for the exchange sense, while mutual also covers shared possession.
entries.definitionCN: 相互给予或做出的。它是“交换”义的严格说法，而 mutual 还覆盖“共同拥有”。

entries.definition: belonging to or shared by several. It states joint possession without any idea of giving and receiving.
entries.definitionCN: 共有的；共同使用的。它只说明共同拥有，不含给予与接受的意思。

entries.definition: done or shared by two or more parties acting together, as in a joint statement.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同做出或共享的，如 joint statement（联合声明）。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin stem mut-, the mutare family of mutable and mutation, and the documented history of mutual friend, mutual fund and MAD.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁词干 mut-、mutable 与 mutation 所属的 mutare 词族，以及 mutual friend、mutual fund、MAD 有据可查的历史。

normal.en: Picture an exchange: one hand gives a key, the other hand gives a key back. That is the original sense, 'reciprocally given and received'.
normal.cn: 想象一次交换：一只手递出钥匙，另一只手也递回钥匙。这就是本义“相互给予并接受”。

normal.en: Mutable, mutation and commute all carry Latin mutare 'to change'; mutual carries the same stem for an exchange of things or feelings.
normal.cn: mutable、mutation、commute 都带拉丁语 mutare“改变”；mutual 用同一词干表示物品或情感的交换。

normal.en: A mutual friend is a person both parties know, which is why critics call the phrase a loose use of 'common'.
normal.cn: a mutual friend 是两方都认识的人，正因如此，批评者说这个短语是对 common 的宽松误用。

normal.en: A mutual fund pools money, and mutual insurance pools risk: both are modern institutions built on shared ownership.
normal.cn: mutual fund 汇集资金，mutual insurance 汇集风险：两者都是建立在共同所有权上的现代制度。

normal.en: The standard frames are mutual respect, mutual understanding, mutual benefit and mutual agreement.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是 mutual respect、mutual understanding、mutual benefit 与 mutual agreement。

abstract.en: Two arrows drawn head to head: each direction needs the other, and a single arrow would not be mutual.
abstract.cn: 画两支箭头对着彼此：每个方向都需要另一边，只画一支就不叫 mutual。

abstract.en: A two-pan balance with equal weights: nothing tips, because what is given on one side is returned on the other.
abstract.cn: 一架两盘天平，两边砝码相等：哪边都不下沉，因为一边给出的在另一边被回敬。

abstract.en: Take one partner away and the word loses its point: mutual always needs a second party in the picture.
abstract.cn: 拿走一方，这个词就失去意义：mutual 的画面里永远需要一个“另一方”。

examples.en: The two countries signed the treaty out of mutual interest, not friendship.
examples.cn: 两国签署这项条约是出于共同利益，而非友谊。

examples.en: Mutual respect kept the debate civil even when the disagreement was sharp.
examples.cn: 相互尊重让这场辩论即使分歧尖锐也保持文明。

examples.en: They were introduced by a mutual friend who knew both families.
examples.cn: 他们是由一位认识两家人的共同朋友引见的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谬球」——两人把同一个球互相抛来抛去，你抛给我、我抛给你 → mutual 相互的、彼此的

root: 源自拉丁语 mutuus“相互的、交换而成的”，可追溯至原始印欧语 *mei-(1)“改变、移动”，核心是双方交换，而非共同拥有。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of mutual all grow from one picture: two parties handing something to each other. From exchanged feeling it extends to shared possession, then to contracts, member-owned institutions, formal relations and finally to the deadly symmetry of MAD.
sensesIntro.cn: mutual 的十个义项都从同一幅画生长出来：两方把东西递给对方。从被交换的情感，它扩展到共同拥有，再扩展到契约、会员共有的机构、形式关系，最后到 MAD 那种致命的对称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands passing the same key to each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一把钥匙互相递过去。

branches.en: THE EXCHANGE CORE: reciprocal action and reciprocal feeling, the oldest and strictest sense.
branches.cn: 交换核心：相互的行为与相互的情感，最古老也最严格的义项。

branches.en: SHARED, NOT EXCHANGED: the disputed mutual friend and the wider 'common' sense.
branches.cn: 共享而非交换：备受争议的 mutual friend，以及更宽的“共同”义。

branches.en: BENEFIT AND CONTRACT: advantage that runs both ways, and promises that bind both sides.
branches.cn: 利益与契约：双向流动的好处，以及约束双方的承诺。

branches.en: POOLED OWNERSHIP: member-owned insurance and the mutual fund, where sharing becomes an institution.
branches.cn: 汇聚式所有权：会员共有的保险与共同基金，共享在此变成制度。

branches.en: FORMAL SYMMETRY: mutual entailment in logic and the mutual destruction of the nuclear standoff.
branches.cn: 形式对称：逻辑中的相互蕴含，以及核对峙中的相互摧毁。

intro.en: Mutual is Latin mutuus plus the adjective suffix -al. English then builds mutually, mutuality, mutualism, mutualist, mutualize and mutualization, while the bare stem mut- lives on in mutation, mutable and commute.
intro.cn: mutual 是拉丁语 mutuus 加形容词后缀 -al。英语随后构造出 mutually、mutuality、mutualism、mutualist、mutualize 与 mutualization，而光秃的词干 mut- 仍活在 mutation、mutable、commute 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutuus 'reciprocal, done in exchange' is the direct source; the same stem gives mutare 'to change' and commutare 'to exchange'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mutuus“相互的、交换而成的”是直接来源；同一词干还给出 mutare“改变”与 commutare“交换”。

items.meaningCN: 相互的；双方共享的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The agreement rests on mutual trust.
items.exampleCN: 这项协议建立在相互信任之上。

items.meaning: in a reciprocal way, each toward the other
items.meaningCN: 相互地；彼此地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two plans are mutually exclusive.

items.meaningCN: 相互性；共同性（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The contract depends on the mutuality of the promises.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同依赖于承诺的相互性。

items.meaning: a system of mutual dependence, or a symbiotic partnership
items.meaningCN: 互助主义；互利共生（-ism 构成体系名词）
items.example: Certain ants and plants live in mutualism.
items.exampleCN: 某些蚂蚁与植物处于互利共生关系。

items.meaning: a supporter of mutualism, or an organism in a mutual partnership
items.meaningCN: 互助主义者；互利共生的一方（-ist 构成人或形容词）
items.example: The coral and its algae are mutualists.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚与它的藻类是互利共生的一方。

items.meaning: to convert an enterprise into member ownership
items.meaningCN: 使共有；转为互助制（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The society voted to mutualize the savings bank.
items.exampleCN: 该协会投票决定把储蓄银行转为互助制。

items.meaningCN: 共有化；互助化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Mutualization changed how the insurer was governed.
items.exampleCN: 互助化改变了这家保险公司的治理方式。

items.meaning: a change of form or genetic material
items.example: The mutation gave the moths a darker wing.
items.exampleCN: 这次突变让蛾子的翅膀变深了。

items.meaningCN: 易变的；可改变的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: Language is mutable, and slang changes fastest.
items.exampleCN: 语言是可变的，而俚语变化最快。

items.meaning: to travel regularly, or to exchange one penalty for another
items.meaningCN: 通勤；减刑（com-“共同、交换”+ mut-“改变”）
items.example: She commutes by train every morning.
items.exampleCN: 她每天早上乘火车通勤。

definition_zh: 我的；用于感叹或称呼
definition_en: belonging to the speaker; also used in exclamations and in polite forms of address
core_image: 一只手把一件东西按在自己胸前，表示这件东西归我
scene: 门口的木架上挂着两件外套，一件深蓝，一件灰色。My coat is the blue one hanging by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「我的」（第 1 个义项：表示所属）；句意为挂在门边的那件蓝色外套是我的。图中可辨识物件：木架、两件外套、门。

pos.zh: 我的（形容词性物主代词）

derivatives.zh: my 的名词性形式，后面不接名词，义为「我的（东西）」
my 与 self 结合而成的反身代词，义为「我自己」

senses.title: Belonging to the speaker
senses.definition: belonging to the person who is speaking, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 属于说话人，用在名词之前
senses.example: My coat is the blue one hanging by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 挂在门边的那件蓝色外套是我的。
senses.why: Old English min was the genitive of the first person; a shortened form took over before nouns, so the word now points at an owner rather than naming a person.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 min 是第一人称的属格形式；一个缩短的形式在名词前占了上风，于是这个词现在指向所有者，而不是称呼某个人。

senses.title: Used in exclamations
senses.definition: used at the start of an exclamation to show surprise or dismay
senses.definitionCN: 放在感叹句开头，表示惊讶或不安
senses.example: My goodness, that was a close call.
senses.exampleCN: 天哪，刚才真是好险。
senses.why: The owner word became a way to put the speaker at the centre of a reaction, so my goodness means the surprise belongs to me, not to the thing seen.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示所有者的词变成了把说话人放在反应中心的手段，所以 my goodness 意味着惊讶属于我，而不是属于看到的东西。

senses.title: Used in polite address
senses.titleCN: 用于称呼（如亲爱的、大人）
senses.definition: used before a title or a term of address in courteous or old-fashioned speech
senses.definitionCN: 用于礼貌或老派的称呼之前
senses.example: My dear friend, you have nothing to worry about.
senses.exampleCN: 亲爱的朋友，你没有什么可担心的。
senses.why: A speaker who calls someone my dear marks that person as belonging to his circle of care, which is why the owner word turned into a marker of warmth.
senses.whyCN: 说话人叫对方 my dear，是把对方划进自己关心的圈子，这个表所属的词因此变成了表示亲切的标记。

intro.en: My is the genitive of the English first person, shortened from an Old English form that also produced mine.
intro.cn: my 是英语第一人称的属格形式，由古英语的一个形式缩短而来，mine 也出自同一来源。

items.en: A first person stem reconstructed with the shape me- is generally taken as the source of the possessive forms across the family.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构为 me- 的第一人称词干是整个语族中各种所有格形式的来源。

items.en: The possessive was reconstructed as minaz, marked for the speaker and agreeing with the thing owned.
items.cn: 所有格被重构为 minaz，既标记说话人，也随被拥有之物变化。

items.en: Old English used min before nouns and as a standalone form, with different endings for gender and number.
items.cn: 古英语用 min 放在名词前，也可单独使用，并随性与数变化词尾。

items.en: Middle English shortened min to mi before consonants and kept mine before vowels, a pattern still visible in the modern pair.
items.cn: 中古英语在辅音前把 min 缩成 mi，在元音前保留 mine，这一分别仍留在现代的一对形式里。

items.en: Modern English fixed my before nouns and mine on its own, and the two stopped differing by the following sound.
items.cn: 现代英语固定为名词前用 my、单独用 mine，两者不再随后面音素区分。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the nominal possessive and the reflexive built on the same stem, plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group collects other possessives.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的名词性所有格与反身代词，另加一个只是外形相似的词；近义组收其他所有格形式。

entries.definition: The possessive used without a following noun.
entries.definitionCN: 后面不接名词的名词性所有格，义为「我的」。

entries.definition: The object form of the first person singular.
entries.definitionCN: 第一人称单数的宾格形式。

entries.definition: The reflexive pronoun built from the same possessive stem.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一所有格词干构成的反身代词。

entries.definition: Short sight, from a Greek word for squinting; only the opening looks alike.
entries.definitionCN: 近视，源自希腊语「眯眼」；只是开头拼写相似，词源不同。

entries.definition: Belonging to the speaker together with others.
entries.definitionCN: 属于说话人以及其他人；我们的。

entries.definition: Belonging to the person spoken to.
entries.definitionCN: 属于听话的人；你的。

entries.definition: Belonging to people or things already mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已提到的人或物；他们的。

entries.definition: Belonging to a male person already mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已提到的男性；他的。

normalIntro.en: The word is the short form of an Old English possessive, and its longer relative survives as mine and inside myself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语所有格的缩短形式，较长的形态仍以 mine 以及 myself 的组成部分存活。

normal.en: Old English min became mi before consonants and my in modern spelling, so my and mine are two shapes of one word.
normal.cn: 古英语 min 在辅音前变成 mi，后来写作 my，所以 my 与 mine 是同一个词的两个形态。

normal.en: My must stand before a noun; standing alone it becomes mine: my book, but the book is mine.
normal.cn: my 必须放在名词前；单独使用要变 mine：说 my book，但说 the book is mine。

normal.en: My takes no plural and no gender; unlike Latin meus, it never changes for the thing owned.
normal.cn: my 没有复数，也不分性别；不像拉丁语 meus，它从不随被拥有之物变形。

normal.en: My goodness and my word are fixed exclamations, not statements about owning anything.
normal.cn: my goodness 与 my word 是固定的感叹语，不是在陈述拥有什么。

normal.en: In my dear and my lord the word marks closeness or rank, a use that goes back to forms of address.
normal.cn: 在 my dear 与 my lord 里，这个词标记亲近或身份，这种用法来自称呼语。

abstract.en: A hand pressed to the chest says ownership is measured from the speaker outward.
abstract.cn: 一只手按在胸前，说明「所有」是从说话人向外量出来的。

abstract.en: A single letter added to a name turns a person into a position in someone else's life.
abstract.cn: 一个称呼前加上这个词，就把一个人变成了另一个人生活里的位置。

abstract.en: English possessives are short because the speaker is never far from what is claimed.
abstract.cn: 英语的所有格都很短，因为说话人离自己所声称的东西从来不远。

examples.en: My notes are on the kitchen table.
examples.cn: 我的笔记在厨房桌上。

examples.en: My grandmother taught me to sew.
examples.cn: 我外婆教我缝纫。

examples.en: I have lost my keys again.
examples.cn: 我又把钥匙弄丢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买」——my 读音近「买」，我的东西都是我买的。

root: 古英语 min（我的，第一人称属格）缩短为 my；与拉丁语 meus、希腊语词干 me- 同出原始印欧语第一人称词干。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ownership anchored in the speaker; the other senses stretch that anchor into exclamations and forms of address.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「以说话人为锚点的所有」；其余义项把这个锚点伸向感叹语与称呼语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing an object to the chest, marking it as mine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把物件按在胸前，标记它归我。

branches.en: a blue coat claimed at the door
branches.cn: 在门口被认领的蓝色外套

branches.en: a name written on a school bag
branches.cn: 写在书包上的名字

branches.en: hands raised at a near miss
branches.cn: 险些出事时抬起的手

branches.en: a breath let out after a shock
branches.cn: 受惊之后呼出的一口气

branches.en: a greeting spoken to an old friend
branches.cn: 对老朋友说出的问候

intro.en: The word is one short English form of a possessive stem that also yields the standalone form and the reflexive.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语所有格词干的一个短形态，同一词干还产出单独使用的形式和反身代词。

latinIntro.en: Latin carries the same first person stem in its possessive, which inflects for gender where English my does not.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的所有格带着同一个第一人称词干，并且随性别变化，而英语的 my 不变。

definition_zh: 我自己；我本人；独自
definition_en: the reflexive pronoun for the speaker, used when the speaker is the object, for emphasis, or in the phrase by myself meaning alone
core_image: 镜子里的人抬手，镜外的手也同时抬起，两边是同一个人
scene: 厨房里，砧板和菜刀摆在水池边，洋葱刚切到一半。I cut myself while chopping onions for dinner.
sceneCN: 这里是「我自己」（第 1 个义项：反身用法，动作回到主语本身）；句意为切洋葱做晚饭时我割伤了自己。图中可辨识物件：砧板、菜刀、洋葱。

derivatives.zh: myself 中的 self 部分，义为「自身、自我」
由 self 加 -ish 构成，义为「自私的」
由 self 加 -less 构成，义为「无私的」

senses.title: The speaker as the object of his own action
senses.definition: used as the object when the subject and the object are the same speaker
senses.definitionCN: 主语和宾语是同一个人（说话人）时用作宾语
senses.example: I cut myself while chopping onions for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 切洋葱做晚饭时我割伤了自己。
senses.why: English marks a returning action with a compound of the owner word and self, so the doer appears a second time inside the sentence as the one acted on.
senses.whyCN: 英语用「所有者词加 self」的复合形式标记回到自身的动作，于是动作发出者在句中第二次出现，成了被作用的人。

senses.title: The speaker, emphasized
senses.definition: used after a noun or at the end of a clause to stress that it was the speaker and no one else
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词后或句末，强调是说话人本人而不是别人
senses.example: I built these shelves myself.
senses.exampleCN: 这些架子是我自己搭的。
senses.why: The same compound can stand outside the verb's arguments and simply point at the speaker, which turns a reflexive into a spotlight.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合形式可以站在动词论元之外，单纯指向说话人，于是反身代词变成了一束追光。

senses.title: Alone, without company
senses.definition: used with by to say that the speaker is without other people
senses.definitionCN: 与 by 连用，表示身边没有别人
senses.example: I went to the cinema by myself.
senses.exampleCN: 我一个人去看了电影。
senses.why: If the speaker is the only one present, the returning self has no one else to lean on, so the reflexive phrase comes to mean solitude.
senses.whyCN: 如果只有说话人在场，那个回到自身的「我」没有别人可以依靠，反身短语于是引申出「独处」的意思。

intro.en: Myself joins the English possessive my to self, a Germanic word for one's own person that Old English already used in reflexive compounds.
intro.cn: myself 把英语所有格 my 与 self 结合；self 是日耳曼语中表示「自身」的词，古英语已用它构成反身复合形式。

items.en: A stem reconstructed as selbho- is often proposed for the reflexive family, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 常有人为这一族反身词提出重构形式 selbho-，但该重构并不确定。

items.en: The adjective selbaz meant the same person or the very one, and it supplied the base for self.
items.cn: 形容词 selbaz 意为「同一个人、正是那个人」，为 self 提供了基础。

items.en: Old English seolf or self could stand alone as a pronoun and appear in compounds with possessive forms.
items.cn: 古英语 seolf 或 self 可单独作代词，也能与所有格形式组合。

items.en: Middle English wrote combinations such as mi self as two words, and the pattern spread to every person of the pronoun.
items.cn: 中古英语把 mi self 这类组合写成两个词，这一模式扩展到人称代词的每一人称。

items.en: Modern English fused the parts into myself, added the emphatic and the by-phrase uses, and kept the plural pattern ourselves.
items.cn: 现代英语把两部分合并为 myself，发展出强调用法和 by 短语用法，并保留了复数形式 ourselves。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the parallel reflexives for other persons; the near-meaning group holds the bare pronouns and the idea of being alone.
note.cn: 形近组收其他人称的平行反身代词；近义组收不带 self 的代词以及「独自一人」这层意思。

entries.definition: The reflexive for the person spoken to, built the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 听话人的反身代词，构造方式相同。

entries.definition: The reflexive for a male third person.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称男性的反身代词。

entries.definition: The reflexive for we, with the plural selves.
entries.definitionCN: we 的反身代词，用复数形式 selves。

entries.definition: The reflexive for it, used for things and animals.
entries.definitionCN: it 的反身代词，用于事物和动物。

entries.definition: The plain object pronoun, used where the action does not return.
entries.definitionCN: 普通的宾格代词，动作不回到自身时使用。

entries.definition: The subject pronoun that myself points back to.
entries.definitionCN: 主格代词，myself 所指回的对象。

entries.definition: The general reflexive for an unspecified person.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某人的反身代词。

entries.definition: Without other people present, the sense carried by by myself.
entries.definitionCN: 身边没有别人，即 by myself 所表达的意思。

normalIntro.en: The word is my plus self, and the same recipe is repeated across the whole pronoun system.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 my 加 self，同一配方在人称代词的整套系统里反复使用。

normal.en: My plus self gives myself; the plural keeps the same recipe and changes my to our: ourselves.
normal.cn: my 加 self 得到 myself；复数沿用同一配方，把 my 换成 our，得到 ourselves。

normal.en: When the subject and the object are the same person, English uses the self form: I hurt myself, not I hurt me.
normal.cn: 主语和宾语是同一个人时，英语用带 self 的形式：说 I hurt myself，不说 I hurt me。

normal.en: Myself cannot be the subject of a finite verb; emphasis uses I myself or a final myself instead.
normal.cn: myself 不能充当限定动词的主语；要强调可以用 I myself，或把 myself 放在句末。

normal.en: By myself means alone; beside myself means out of control, not standing next to the body.
normal.cn: by myself 意为独自；beside myself 意为情绪失控，而不是站在身体旁边。

normal.en: In including myself, the self form works after a preposition or at the end of a list.
normal.cn: 在 including myself 里，这个反身形式用在介词后或列表末尾。

abstract.en: A mirror is the plainest picture of a sentence that turns back on its speaker.
abstract.cn: 镜子是一个句子折回说话人时最直白的画面。

abstract.en: A spotlight aimed at one person explains the emphatic use better than any rule.
abstract.cn: 一束只照一个人的追光，比任何规则都更能解释强调用法。

abstract.en: An empty cinema seat makes the meaning of by myself visible at once.
abstract.cn: 一个空着的电影院座位，一眼就能让人看见 by myself 的含义。

examples.en: I taught myself to play the guitar.
examples.cn: 我自学弹吉他。

examples.en: I painted the whole fence myself.
examples.cn: 整道栅栏都是我自己刷的。

examples.en: I waited by myself for over an hour.
examples.cn: 我独自等了一个多小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买赛尔夫」——自己给自己买东西，就叫 myself，我自己。

root: my 与古英语 self（自身）复合而成；self 一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 selbaz，拉丁语 ipse 只是意义相近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the speaker turning back on the speaker; emphasis and solitude are two ways that turn becomes visible.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是说话人把动作折回自己；强调用法与独处义，是这一折返的两种显形方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised before a mirror, with the reflected hand rising at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜前抬起一只手，镜中的手在同一刻也抬起。

branches.en: a cut finger held under the tap
branches.cn: 在水龙头下按住割伤的手指

branches.en: a sentence whose object is its subject
branches.cn: 宾语与主语是同一个人的句子

branches.en: a shelf built without help
branches.cn: 没有帮手也照样搭好的架子

branches.en: a ticket bought for one seat only
branches.cn: 只买了一个座位的票

branches.en: an empty row in a dark cinema
branches.cn: 黑暗影院里空着的一排座位

intro.en: The word is a compound of the possessive my and the Germanic self, and the same pieces recur in every reflexive pronoun.
intro.cn: 这个词由所有格 my 与日耳曼语的 self 复合而成，同样的部件在每个人称的反身代词中都会重现。

latinIntro.en: Latin has a reflexive pronoun of its own, but no form of it is a reliable source for self, so the cognate list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语有自己的反身代词，但其中没有任何形式可以可靠地作为 self 的来源，因此同源词列表留空。

items.meaning: the speaker as object or emphasis

definition_zh: 神秘的；难以解释的；讳莫如深的
definition_en: strange and difficult to explain; having a hidden or supernatural quality; deliberately keeping things unclear
core_image: 一扇只开一条缝的门，缝里透出一点看不清的光
scene: 村口的老宅多年无人居住，夜里楼上的窗子却总亮着。The old house keeps a mysterious light burning in its upper window.
sceneCN: 这里是「神秘的、难以解释的」（第 1 个义项：来路不明、说不清楚）；句意为那座老宅楼上窗里始终亮着一盏莫名的灯。图中可辨识物件：老宅、亮着的窗、夜色。

pos.zh: 神秘的；难以解释的；讳莫如深的

derivatives.zh: 由 mysterious 加 -ly 构成，义为「神秘地」
由 mysterious 加 -ness 构成，义为「神秘性」
与 mysterious 同出希腊语词根，义为「谜；神秘事物」

senses.title: Strange and hard to explain
senses.definition: difficult to understand or explain because the facts are hidden
senses.definitionCN: 因事实被遮蔽而难以理解或解释
senses.example: The old house keeps a mysterious light burning in its upper window.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老宅楼上窗里始终亮着一盏莫名的灯。
senses.why: Greek myein meant to close the lips or the eyes, so the family of words starts from what is shut away from view and only later describes how such a thing feels.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 myein 意为闭口或闭眼，因此这一族词的起点是「被关在视线之外的东西」，之后才用来形容这种东西给人的感觉。

senses.title: Touching on hidden or supernatural power
senses.titleCN: 带有神秘力量的；玄秘的
senses.definition: having a quality that seems to come from a hidden or supernatural source
senses.definitionCN: 带有似乎来自隐秘或超自然来源的性质
senses.example: The valley was said to hold mysterious forces that spoiled milk overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 据说那条山谷里有神秘的力量，能让牛奶一夜之间变坏。
senses.why: The word first named secret religious rites open only to the initiated; that closed door of ritual left it with a permanent air of the beyond.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指名只有入会者才能参加的秘仪；仪式那扇关着的门，让它永久带上了一层超验的气息。

senses.title: Deliberately unclear about something
senses.titleCN: 讳莫如深的；故意不说清
senses.definition: choosing to keep one's actions or intentions vague on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意把自己的行为或意图说得含糊
senses.example: She was mysterious about where the money had come from.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这笔钱的来路讳莫如深。
senses.why: Anyone who refuses to explain looks, from outside, exactly like a thing that cannot be explained, so the adjective moves from the unknown object to the person hiding it.
senses.whyCN: 一个人拒绝解释，从外面看就和一件无法解释的东西一模一样，于是这个形容词从被未知的对象转到了藏起它的人身上。

intro.en: Mysterious comes through French from Latin, where the noun had already travelled from Greek rites closed to outsiders.
intro.cn: mysterious 经法语来自拉丁语，而拉丁语中那个名词早已从「不许外人参与的希腊仪式」一路传来。

items.en: The verb myein meant to close, especially the eyes or the lips, and it gave the family its sense of shutting away.
items.cn: 动词 myein 意为闭合，尤指闭眼或闭嘴，为这一族词提供了「关起来、不示人」的意思。

items.en: A mysterion was a secret rite or doctrine revealed only to those admitted to it.
items.cn: mysterion 指只向获准入会者揭示的秘密仪式或教义。

items.en: Latin took the word as mysterium, keeping both the ritual sense and the broader sense of a secret.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词写作 mysterium，既保留仪式义，也泛指秘密。

items.en: French formed the adjective mysterieux from the same stem, and it carried the sense of something unexplained rather than something sacred.
items.cn: 法语用同一词干造出形容词 mysterieux，词义已偏向「说不清的事」，不再限于神圣之事。

items.en: English adopted the French adjective, respelled it with ous, and extended it to people who refuse to explain themselves.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语形容词，改写成带 ous 的形式，并把词义扩展到「不肯解释自己的人」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun, the adverb and other words on the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what cannot be explained.
note.cn: 形近组收同出希腊词根的名词、副词及其他同族词；近义组收表示「无法解释」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for something unexplained or kept secret.
entries.definitionCN: 表示无法解释或被人保密之事的名称。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that cannot be explained.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「神秘地、莫名其妙地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being strange and unexplained.
entries.definitionCN: 神秘、难以解释的性质。

entries.definition: To puzzle someone completely, from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 使人完全困惑，同出这一词干。

entries.definition: A person who seeks direct union with the divine.
entries.definitionCN: 追求与神直接合一的人；神秘的。

entries.definition: Unusual and hard to account for, but without the hint of hidden meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常、难以说明，但没有「背后另有隐情」的暗示。

entries.definition: Hard to understand because the pieces do not fit.
entries.definitionCN: 因线索拼不起来而令人费解。

entries.definition: Deliberately or naturally hard to read, like a riddle.
entries.definitionCN: 像谜语一样难以看透，可指有意为之。

entries.definition: Simply not yet accounted for, without any aura.
entries.definitionCN: 只是尚未得到解释，不带神秘气氛。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective of a Greek noun for closed rites, and its relatives still circle around secrets.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中表示秘仪的名词的形容词形式，它的同族词至今仍围绕「秘密」打转。

normal.en: Greek myein meant to close the eyes or lips, so mysterious begins with the image of a mouth kept shut.
normal.cn: 希腊语 myein 意为闭上眼或闭上嘴，所以 mysterious 的起点是一张闭紧的嘴。

normal.en: Mystery is the noun and mysterious the adjective; adding ous turns a secret into a quality.
normal.cn: mystery 是名词，mysterious 是形容词；加上 ous，就把一个秘密变成了一种性质。

normal.en: The ending is said quickly as -əs, which is why the last syllable almost disappears in speech.
normal.cn: 词尾读得很轻，接近 -əs，所以最后一个音节在口语里几乎听不见。

normal.en: Mystify is the verb of the same family: to make someone feel they are facing a closed door.
normal.cn: mystify 是同一族的动词：让人觉得自己面对的是一扇关着的门。

normal.en: Mysterious circumstances and a mysterious smile both keep the facts just out of reach.
normal.cn: mysterious circumstances 与 a mysterious smile 都让事实停在伸手够不到的地方。

abstract.en: A door left ajar is more disturbing than a door locked tight, because the gap promises something behind it.
abstract.cn: 虚掩的门比紧锁的门更让人不安，因为那道缝许诺了门后有东西。

abstract.en: Every closed rite and every unopened letter teaches the same lesson about hidden knowledge.
abstract.cn: 每一场闭门仪式、每一封未拆的信，都在讲同一件关于隐秘知识的事。

abstract.en: A word that began with shut lips ends by describing the face of someone who will not answer.
abstract.cn: 一个从「闭紧嘴唇」开始的词，最后用来形容一张不肯回答的脸。

examples.en: A mysterious figure was seen near the gate last night.
examples.cn: 昨夜有人在门附近看见一个神秘的身影。

examples.en: The case remains mysterious after thirty years.
examples.cn: 三十年后这桩案子依然扑朔迷离。

examples.en: He gave a mysterious smile and changed the subject.
examples.cn: 他神秘地笑了笑，换了话题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯特瑞斯」——把秘密密起来，脸上就带出神秘；mysterious 就是神秘的。

root: 希腊语 myein（闭口、闭眼）构成 mysterion（秘仪），经拉丁语 mysterium 与法语 mysterieux 进入英语；一般认为词根与「闭合」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what is shut away from view; the senses spread from unexplained events to sacred hidden power and to people who hide their own reasons.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被关在视线之外」；义项从无法解释的事件，扩展到隐秘的神圣力量，再转到有意藏起自己理由的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opened only a crack, with a light inside that cannot be made out.
core.cn: 核心意象：只开一道缝的门，里面有看不清的光。

branches.en: a lamp left burning in an empty house
branches.cn: 空屋里一直亮着的灯

branches.en: a footprint that stops halfway across a room
branches.cn: 走到房间中间就断掉的脚印

branches.en: a rite held behind a curtain
branches.cn: 帘子后面举行的仪式

branches.en: milk souring overnight in a valley
branches.cn: 山谷里一夜变坏的牛奶

branches.en: an answer that slides away from the question
branches.cn: 绕开问题的回答

intro.en: The word is built from a Greek verb of closing, its noun of secret rites, a Latin borrowing, and an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语表「闭合」的动词、其表示秘仪的名词、拉丁语的借形，以及一个英语形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek noun as mysterium and formed mysticus from the same root, and both stand behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语名词借作 mysterium，又用同一词根造出 mysticus，两者都支撑着英语这一族词。
