definition_zh: 谜；神秘事物；神秘气氛；悬疑作品
definition_en: something that cannot be explained or is kept secret; the quality of being secret; a story built around an unsolved puzzle
core_image: 一只上锁的抽屉，里面的东西不翼而飞，锁却完好无损
scene: 书房的抽屉少了一封信，锁面没有撬痕，窗子也从里面扣着。The letter vanished from a locked drawer, and the mystery is still unsolved.
sceneCN: 这里是「谜、无法解释的事」（第 1 个义项：找不到答案的事件）；句意为信从上锁的抽屉里消失，这个谜至今未解。图中可辨识物件：抽屉、锁、信、窗扣。

pos.zh: 谜；神秘事物；神秘气氛；悬疑作品

derivatives.zh: 由 mystery 的词干加 -ous 构成，义为「神秘的」
由 mysterious 加 -ly 构成，义为「神秘地」
由同一词干加 -ify 构成，义为「使困惑不解」
由 mystic 加 -ism 构成，义为「神秘主义」

senses.title: Something that cannot be explained
senses.definition: a fact or event that resists explanation and keeps people guessing
senses.definitionCN: 无法解释、让人不断猜测的事实或事件
senses.example: The letter vanished from a locked drawer, and the mystery is still unsolved.
senses.exampleCN: 信从上锁的抽屉里消失，这个谜至今未解。
senses.why: The Greek noun named rites closed to outsiders; once the ritual frame fell away, what remained was a fact shut off from explanation, which is the everyday sense today.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词本指不许外人参加的仪式；仪式的外壳脱落之后，剩下的就是一个被挡在解释之外的事实，也就是今天的日常义。

senses.title: The quality of being secret or strange
senses.definition: an atmosphere of secrecy that surrounds a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 笼罩在人、地点或事物周围的神秘气息
senses.example: An air of mystery hangs over the house at the end of the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 巷子尽头那座房子笼罩着一层神秘气息。
senses.why: Because the word names what is withheld, it can also name the withheld quality itself, so a place becomes mysterious by carrying a mystery rather than by containing one.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指被扣住不说的东西，它也能指那种被扣住的性质本身，于是一个地方不必真的藏着什么谜，只要带着谜的气息就显得神秘。

senses.title: A story built around a puzzle
senses.definition: a book, film or play whose plot turns on an unexplained event and its solution
senses.definitionCN: 以未解事件及其解答为主线的小说、电影或戏剧
senses.example: She reads a murder mystery every week before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周睡前读一本谋杀悬疑小说。
senses.why: Readers wanted the pleasure of a puzzle that gets solved, so the word moved from the puzzle itself to the kind of book that delivers one.
senses.whyCN: 读者想要的是「谜被解开」的快感，于是这个词从谜本身转到了提供这种谜的那类书。

intro.en: Mystery reached English through Old French from Latin, and the Latin noun had already borrowed a Greek word for rites open only to the initiated.
intro.cn: mystery 经古法语、拉丁语进入英语，而拉丁语名词此前已借入一个希腊词，指只许入会者参加的仪式。

items.en: The verb myein meant to close, especially the lips or the eyes, and the sense of shutting away runs through the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 myein 意为闭合，尤指闭嘴或闭眼，这一族词始终带着「关起来」的意思。

items.en: A mysterion was a secret rite or teaching that insiders guarded from outsiders.
items.cn: mysterion 指内部人对外人守口如瓶的秘密仪式或教义。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as mysterium, where the sense widened from a rite to any hidden matter.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 mysterium，词义从仪式扩大到任何隐秘之事。

items.en: Old French mistere carried both the religious sense and the sense of a hidden truth, and passed the word to English.
items.cn: 古法语 mistere 兼有宗教义与「隐秘真相」义，并把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the puzzle sense, adds the atmosphere sense and the name of a literary genre.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「谜」义，又添上「气氛」义，并把词用作一类文学体裁的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective, the verb and other relatives on the same stem; the near-meaning group holds words for puzzles and secrets.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形容词、动词及其他同族词；近义组收表示谜题与秘密的词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing what cannot be explained.
entries.definitionCN: 形容无法解释之事的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb for something done in an unexplained way.
entries.definitionCN: 表示以难以解释的方式。

entries.definition: To baffle someone, as if by a closed door.
entries.definitionCN: 使人困惑，仿佛面对一扇关着的门。

entries.definition: The belief that the divine can be reached directly.
entries.definitionCN: 认为可以直接抵达神性的信仰。

entries.definition: A traditional story about gods or origins; the similarity is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 关于神或起源的传统故事；只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A problem that needs thought before it can be solved.
entries.definitionCN: 需要思考才能解决的问题。

entries.definition: A fact kept from others on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意不让他人知道的事实。

entries.definition: A question or object whose meaning is deliberately hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 含义被有意藏起来的提问或物件。

entries.definition: A person or thing that is impossible to read.
entries.definitionCN: 无法看透的人或事物。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a name for closed rites and now covers any unexplained fact, the feeling around it, and the books written about it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是闭门仪式的名称，如今覆盖任何无法解释的事实、围绕它的感觉，以及以此为题材的书。

normal.en: The word goes back to Greek myein, to close the lips; a mystery is something someone keeps their mouth shut about.
normal.cn: 这个词可追到希腊语 myein（闭嘴）；mystery 就是有人闭口不谈的事。

normal.en: The plural is mysteries, with y changing to ies, the same pattern as story and stories.
normal.cn: 复数是 mysteries，y 变 ies，与 story、stories 的变化方式相同。

normal.en: Mystery is the noun, mysterious the adjective, mystify the verb; the family keeps one stem and changes only the ending.
normal.cn: mystery 是名词，mysterious 是形容词，mystify 是动词；这一族共用同一词干，只换词尾。

normal.en: An air of mystery needs no hidden fact; it can be produced by a closed door and a dim lamp.
normal.cn: an air of mystery 并不需要真藏着什么；一扇关着的门和一盏昏暗的灯就能造出它。

normal.en: A murder mystery is a genre label, so the word can name a shelf in a bookshop as well as a puzzle in a locked room.
normal.cn: a murder mystery 是体裁标签，所以这个词既能指密室里的谜，也能指书店里的一个书架。

abstract.en: A locked drawer with nothing missing teaches that a question can outlast its answer.
abstract.cn: 一只什么都没丢的上锁抽屉，说明问题可以比答案活得更久。

abstract.en: Every secret is a room whose door is shut from the inside, and every mystery is the light under that door.
abstract.cn: 每个秘密都是从里面关上的房间，而每个谜都是门缝下透出的光。

abstract.en: A word that names a closed rite ends up naming the pleasure of watching a lock be picked.
abstract.cn: 一个命名闭门仪式的词，最后用来命名「看别人开锁」的乐趣。

examples.en: The cause of the fire remains a mystery.
examples.cn: 起火的原因仍然是个谜。

examples.en: He enjoys solving mysteries set in old hotels.
examples.cn: 他喜欢破解以老旅馆为背景的谜案。

examples.en: Her sudden departure is shrouded in mystery.
examples.cn: 她的突然离开笼罩在神秘之中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯特瑞」——秘密被锁在密室里，就成了谜；mystery 就是谜。

root: 希腊语 myein（闭口、闭眼）派生的 mysterion（秘仪）经拉丁语 mysterium、古法语 mistere 进入英语；一般认为核心是「对外人闭合」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fact kept behind a closed door; the senses extend to the atmosphere such a fact creates and to stories built on solving it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被关在门后的事实；义项扩展到这种事实造成的气氛，以及以解开它为骨架的故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked drawer standing open with its contents gone and its lock unbroken.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁完好无损，抽屉却开着，里面的东西不见了。

branches.en: a letter missing from a locked drawer
branches.cn: 上锁抽屉里不见了的信

branches.en: a detective holding a key that fits nothing
branches.cn: 拿着一把配不上任何锁的钥匙的侦探

branches.en: a dim lamp behind drawn curtains
branches.cn: 拉上窗帘后的一盏暗灯

branches.en: a house no neighbour will talk about
branches.cn: 邻居都不愿提起的房子

branches.en: a paperback left open at the last page
branches.cn: 摊在最后一页的平装书

intro.en: The word passes from a Greek verb of closing through a Greek noun, a Latin borrowing and an Old French form before it names a puzzle in English.
intro.cn: 这个词从希腊语表「闭合」的动词出发，经希腊名词、拉丁借形与古法语形式，最后在英语里指一个谜。

latinIntro.en: Latin carried the Greek noun into mysterium and also used the plural mysteria for the rites themselves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词带入 mysterium，也用复数 mysteria 指仪式本身。

items.meaning: to close the lips or eyes

definition_zh: 神话；神话故事；神话体系；广为相信的谬见；虚构的人或事；编造的托词
definition_en: a traditional story about gods or origins, or a widely believed but false idea
core_image: 夜里的火堆旁，老人用手比划着天与地如何分开，听的人明知不是真的却仍点头
scene: 火堆旁，老人把陶罐放在膝上，向围坐的孩子讲起天和地最初如何分开。An old storyteller recounts the myth of how sky and earth were separated.
sceneCN: 这里 myth 指「关于神或世界起源的传统故事」（第 1 个义项：世代相传的神话叙事）；句意为一位老讲述者讲述天与地如何分开的神话。可辨识物件：火堆、陶罐、围坐的孩子、夜色；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 神话；神话故事；神话体系；谬见；虚构的人或事

derivatives.zh: 基础词 myth + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 由「神话故事」偏移为「具有神话气质的、传奇般的」
基础词 myth + -ical（形容词后缀）→ 偏移为「只存在于神话中、虚构的」
基础词 myth + 希腊 -logia（「讲述、研究」）→ 由「一则故事」偏移为「神话的整体汇集与研究」
mythology + -ist（人名词后缀）→ 偏移为「研究神话的学者」
mythology + -ize（动词后缀）→ 由「神话」偏移为「把某人某事讲成神话」
mythologize + -ation（动作名词后缀）→ 偏移为「被讲成神话的过程」
myth + maker（英语复合，表制造者）→ 偏移为「编造神话或制造流行谬见的人」

senses.title: A traditional tale of gods
senses.titleCN: 关于神与起源的传统故事
senses.definition: a traditional story, usually concerning gods or the origin of the world, passed on by a community
senses.definitionCN: 通常在讲神或世界起源、由群体世代相传的传统故事
senses.example: The myth tells how the first fire was carried down from the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 这则神话讲的是最初的火如何从山上被带下来。
senses.why: the Greek noun meant a thing spoken aloud, so a myth is first of all a story that a community keeps telling.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词原指被大声讲出来的东西，所以神话首先是一个群体不断讲述的故事。

senses.title: A body of myths
senses.definition: the whole collection of such stories belonging to one culture or subject
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一文化或主题的这类故事的整体汇集
senses.example: The myth of the region is preserved mainly in oral chant.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的神话主要靠口头吟唱保存。
senses.why: the singular noun can stand for a whole tradition, the way a library name stands for all its books.
senses.whyCN: 单数名词可以代表整个传统，就像一座图书馆的名字代表它的全部藏书。

senses.title: A widely believed falsehood
senses.definition: an idea that many people accept as true although it has been shown to be false
senses.definitionCN: 许多人信以为真、但已被证明为假的说法
senses.example: It is a myth that we use only a tenth of the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 「人只用了大脑的十分之一」是一种谬见。
senses.why: a story that everyone repeats can harden into something people treat as fact, and English extended the same noun to that kind of false belief.
senses.whyCN: 一个被所有人反复讲述的故事会硬化成人们当作事实的东西，英语便把同一个名词扩展到这类错误信念上。

senses.title: A fabricated person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that exists only in imagination or in a story
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于想象或故事中的人或物
senses.example: The feared pirate turned out to be a myth invented by the port's guides.
senses.exampleCN: 那个令人惧怕的海盗后来证明是港口导游编出来的虚构人物。
senses.why: a figure that exists only because it is talked about is the same product as a story, with a face attached.
senses.whyCN: 一个只因为被谈论才存在的人物，与一个故事是同一种产物，只是给它安上了一张脸。

senses.title: A made-up excuse
senses.definition: an invented account offered to explain or excuse something
senses.definitionCN: 为解释或开脱某事而编出来的说法
senses.example: His story about a delayed train was pure myth.
senses.exampleCN: 他那套火车误点的说法纯属编造。
senses.why: an excuse is a short story offered in place of the facts, so the same noun serves when the telling is deliberate.
senses.whyCN: 托词是一则用来代替事实的短故事，因此当讲述是故意为之，同一个名词就派上了用场。

senses.title: A category of narrative
senses.titleCN: 神话作为叙事类型（学术用语）
senses.definition: the class of narrative that scholars set apart from legend, folktale and history
senses.definitionCN: 学者用来与传说、民间故事和历史相区分的那类叙事
senses.example: In this discipline, myth is defined by its concern with origins, not by its being false.
senses.exampleCN: 在这门学科里，神话是由它关注起源来定义的，而不是由它虚假来定义的。
senses.why: scholars needed a neutral label for the genre, so the noun was kept but stripped of the everyday judgement that a myth is simply untrue.
senses.whyCN: 学者需要给这一文类一个中性的标签，于是保留了这个名词，却去掉了日常语言里「神话就是假的」那层判断。

senses.title: A legendary figure
senses.titleCN: 传奇式人物，被神化的偶像
senses.definition: a person who has been talked about so much that the telling has replaced the person
senses.definitionCN: 被谈论得太多、以致讲述取代了本人的人物
senses.example: By the end of his career the boxer had become a myth in his own city.
senses.exampleCN: 到职业生涯末期，这位拳手在自己城市里已经成了一个传奇。
senses.why: when the telling grows larger than the person, the story takes over the identity, and the noun names the figure that remains.
senses.whyCN: 当讲述大过本人，故事便接管了这个身份，名词所指的就是剩下的那个形象。

senses.title: A story a society tells itself
senses.definition: a shared narrative that a society uses to explain or justify its own arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会用来解释或为自己制度辩护的共同叙事
senses.example: The frontier myth still shapes how the country explains its history.
senses.exampleCN: 边疆神话至今仍在塑造这个国家解释自身历史的方式。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the story element but shifts the function: the tale now explains the tellers to themselves.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了故事成分，却换了功能：故事现在用来向讲述者自己解释他们自身。

intro.en: Myth comes from Greek mythos 'word, speech, story', borrowed into Late Latin and then into modern languages; English took it through French in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: myth 来自希腊 mythos「言语、讲述、故事」，先借入晚期拉丁，再进入近代诸语言；英语经法语在十九世纪引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mythos covered 'word, speech, thing said, tale'. It could mean a public pronouncement as much as a narrative, so speech and story were one idea.
items.cn: mythos 涵盖「言语、讲述、所说之事、故事」，既可指公开宣告，也可指叙事，说话与故事在当时是一个概念。

items.en: Philosophers set mythos against logos, the reasoned account, and from that contrast mythos acquired the overtone of an unproved story.
items.cn: 哲学家把 mythos 与 logos（理性论证）对立起来，自此 mythos 带上「未经证明的故事」这一色彩。

items.en: Late Latin took mythos as a learned borrowing; it was not an inherited Latin noun and had no Latin relatives of its own.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁把 mythos 作为学术借词吸收；它不是拉丁语固有名词，也没有自身的拉丁同族词。

items.en: French mythe carried the learned word into modern use, and English myth followed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 mythe 把这个学术词带入近代用法，英语的 myth 随后在十九世纪出现。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the noun widened from sacred tales to any widely repeated falsehood, a sense now commoner than the original one.
items.cn: 在十九与二十世纪，这个名词从神圣故事扩展到任何被广泛重复的错误说法，这一义项如今比原义更常用。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of mythos before Greek is not established, and no Indo-European source has been demonstrated; any older form proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：mythos 在希腊语之前的来源未得到证明，也没有任何印欧语来源被证实；凡为它提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates myth from the story genres it is confused with; group two holds the everyday words for untrue or unproved accounts.
note.cn: 第一组把 myth 与常被混淆的故事文类分开；第二组是表示「不实、未经证明」的日常词。

entries.definition: A story about a human hero, often attached to a real place or person; myth deals with gods and origins, legend keeps a historical foothold.
entries.definitionCN: 关于人类英雄的故事，常附着于真实地点或人物；神话处理神与起源，传说则保留历史落脚点。

entries.definition: A story told among ordinary people, often for entertainment or moral instruction; it lacks the sacred and explanatory role of myth.
entries.definitionCN: 在普通民众间讲述的故事，多用于娱乐或教化；它没有神话那种神圣与解释的作用。

entries.definition: A short invented story, often with animals, that points to a moral; it is openly fictional and didactic.
entries.definitionCN: 常以动物为主角的短小虚构故事，指向一条道理；它公开承认虚构并带训诫性。

entries.definition: A collection of myths or the study of them; myth is one story, mythology is the set or the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 神话的汇集或对神话的研究；myth 是一则故事，mythology 是整套或这门学科。

entries.definition: The Greek word itself, used in English for the underlying pattern of a myth or for a group's shared story-world.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊原词本身，在英语中用来指一则神话的底层模式，或一个群体共享的故事世界。

entries.definition: A mistaken understanding held by many people; it names the error plainly, without the story image that myth carries.
entries.definitionCN: 许多人持有的错误理解；它直白地指错误，不含 myth 所带的故事意象。

entries.definition: A statement that is not true, whether or not anyone believes it; myth adds wide acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实的陈述，无论是否有人相信；myth 则多了「被广泛接受」这一层。

entries.definition: Something invented on purpose to deceive; it implies intent, while a myth's false sense often implies only repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 为欺骗而故意编造的东西；它含故意，而 myth 的谬见义常只含反复流传。

entries.definition: The state of holding something as true; a myth may become a belief, but belief itself says nothing about stories.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事当作真的状态；神话可以变成信念，但 belief 本身与故事无关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek elements, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek mythos 'a thing said': a myth is literally something a community keeps saying aloud.
normal.cn: 希腊 mythos「被说出的东西」：神话字面上就是一个群体不断大声讲的东西。

normal.en: The family runs myth, mythic, mythical, mythology, mythologist, mythologize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 myth、mythic、mythical、mythology、mythologist、mythologize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark both senses: ancient myth, Greek myth, and the myth of progress.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出两层意思：古老神话、希腊神话，以及关于进步的虚妄信念。

normal.en: Greek kept mythos and logos as a pair: story against reasoned account.
normal.cn: 希腊语把 mythos 与 logos 当作一对：故事对理性论证。

normal.en: The academic use says myth concerns origins, so a myth can be true to its tellers and still be a myth.
normal.cn: 学术用法说神话关注起源，因此一则神话对讲述者可以为真，却仍然是神话。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that gets heavier each time it is repeated, until it can no longer be lifted.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话每被重复一次就重一点，最后重得抬不起来。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait repainted by every visitor until the original face is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像被每位来客添改，最后原来的脸已经不见了。

abstract.en: Picture a map drawn from memory and then used as if it were the ground itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一张凭记忆画的地图，后来被当成地面本身来使用。

examples.en: The myth explains why the river turns salt where it meets the sea.
examples.cn: 这则神话解释了那条河为什么在人海处变咸。

examples.en: It is a myth that older workers cannot learn new software.
examples.cn: 「年长的员工学不会新软件」是一种谬见。

examples.en: The film turns a minor local trader into a myth of resistance.
examples.cn: 这部影片把一个微不足道的本地商人塑造成了抵抗的传奇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「myth（音近『秘思』）」——被反复讲述、越传越神秘的那套说法 → 神话；也指广为相信的谬见

root: 希腊 mythos「言语、讲述、故事」，先作学术借词进入晚期拉丁，再经法语进入英语；mythos 更早来源不确定，无已证实的印欧语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: something gets told and retold, and the retelling first makes a sacred story, then a whole story-world, then a false belief, an invented person, an excuse, a genre label, a legendary figure, and finally a society's account of itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：某件事被讲了又讲，这反复讲述先造出神圣故事，再造出整套故事世界，随后造出谬见、虚构人物、托词、文类标签、传奇人物，最后造出一个社会对自身的解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tale retold around a fire until the retelling stands where the fact used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：火堆旁被一遍遍重讲的故事，讲到后来，重讲本身站在了事实原来的位置上。

branches.en: THE TALE AND THE SET: one story first, then the whole body of stories a culture keeps.
branches.cn: 故事与整套：先是一则故事，再是一个文化保存的整批故事。

branches.en: REPETITION WITHOUT PROOF: an often-repeated tale turns into a false belief, and an invented account becomes an excuse.
branches.cn: 无凭据的重复：被反复讲述的故事变成错误信念，编出来的说法变成托词。

branches.en: PERSONS MADE OF TALK: a thing or a person can be wholly produced by the telling.
branches.cn: 由讲述造出的人与物：一件东西或一个人可以完全由讲述生产出来。

branches.en: A NEUTRAL GENRE LABEL: scholars keep the noun but drop the judgement that a myth must be false.
branches.cn: 中性的文类标签：学者保留这个名词，却去掉「神话必然虚假」这一判断。

branches.en: THE STORY A SOCIETY TELLS ITSELF: the tale now explains the tellers to themselves.
branches.cn: 社会讲给自己的故事：故事此时用来向讲述者解释他们自身。

intro.en: Myth is a bare Greek noun in English, but it builds a large family through suffixes that name studies, qualities, persons and processes.
intro.cn: myth 在英语里是一个光裸的希腊名词，但它通过指学科、性质、人物与过程的后缀建起一个很大的词族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin family stands behind myth. Latin took mythos only as a Greek loanword, so there is no inherited Latin cognate to list.
latinIntro.cn: myth 背后没有拉丁词族。拉丁语只把 mythos 当作希腊借词吸收，因此没有可列的拉丁固有同族词。

items.example: The myth survived in three versions.
items.exampleCN: 这则神话以三个版本留存下来。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into a quality word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成性质词。

items.example: The longer suffix sounds more formal.
items.exampleCN: 较长的后缀听起来更正式。

items.example: The striker became a mythic name.
items.exampleCN: 这位前锋成了神话般的名字。

items.example: A mythical harbour appears on the old chart.
items.exampleCN: 旧海图上出现一个神话中的港口。

items.meaning: the set of myths or their study
items.meaningCN: 神话的整体或对神话的研究
items.example: She teaches the mythology of northern Europe.

items.exampleCN: 这位神话学者编目了各种异文。
回忆录作者会把自己的青年时代写成神话。

items.example: The mythologization of the founder began at his funeral.
items.exampleCN: 对创始人的神话化从他的葬礼就开始了。

items.meaning: one who invents myths or false beliefs
items.exampleCN: 每个时代都有自己的神话制造者。

definition_zh: 指甲；趾甲；钉子；钉住；逮住
definition_en: the hard plate at the end of a finger or toe; a small metal pin used to fasten things; and, as a verb, to fix something with such a pin or to catch someone
core_image: 锤子落下，一枚小钉被送进木板，只留下一个扁平的钉帽
scene: 修鞋摊的木板上钉着一排旧鞋掌，师傅抬手示意我别碰那块松动的边角。He drove a nail into the loose board so that it would stop rattling.
sceneCN: 这里是「钉子」（第 2 个义项：用来连接或固定木料的金属小钉）；句意是他把一枚钉子钉进松动的木板，好让它不再吱呀作响。图中可辨识物件：钉帽、旧鞋掌、木凳。

collocations.phrase: hit the nail on the head

derivatives.zh: 由 finger 与 nail 复合而成，义为「手指甲」
由 toe 与 nail 复合而成，义为「脚趾甲」
由 nail 与 brush 复合而成，义为「指甲刷」

senses.title: The hard plate at the end of a finger or toe
senses.definition: the hard, smooth layer that grows at the end of a finger or toe and protects the tip
senses.definitionCN: 手指或脚趾末端长出的坚硬平滑层，用来保护指端
senses.example: She kept her nails short so that she could work at the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 为了能在机器旁干活，她把指甲一直剪得很短。
senses.why: Old English nægl named this hard plate first; the metal pin took the same word because both are small, hard and gripping.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nægl 最早指的就是这层硬片；金属钉后来共用同一个词，因为两者都是又小又硬、能把东西咬住的东西。

senses.title: A small metal pin used for fastening
senses.definition: a short metal spike driven into wood or a wall to join pieces or hold something in place
senses.definitionCN: 钉入木头或墙面的短金属钉，用来连接构件或把东西固定住
senses.example: The picture hung from a single nail above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅画就挂在门上方的一枚钉子上。
senses.why: The Germanic word covered both the body's hard plate and the metal peg, so the shared picture is a small hard thing that holds on.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼词同时指身体的硬片和金属小钉，共有的画面就是一件小而硬、能牢牢咬住的东西。

senses.title: To fasten something with a nail
senses.definition: to fix an object in place by driving a nail into it, or to attach one thing to another in this way
senses.definitionCN: 把钉子钉入某物使其固定，或以这种方式把两件东西连接起来
senses.example: They nailed boards over the broken window before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，他们用木板钉住了破掉的窗户。
senses.why: Once the noun names the tool, the verb needs no new idea: it simply names the act of putting that tool to work.
senses.whyCN: 名词既已指这件工具，动词就不需要新意思，只是把「使用这件工具」的动作说出来。

senses.title: To catch or hit exactly
senses.definition: in informal speech, to catch someone, to hit something exactly, or to do something perfectly
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示抓住某人、正好击中某物，或把事情办得无可挑剔
senses.example: The police nailed the driver at the second checkpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在第二个检查站逮住了那个司机。
senses.why: A nail stops a board from moving, so the verb can picture anything pinned down beyond doubt: a suspect caught, a target hit, an answer found.
senses.whyCN: 钉子能止住木板的活动，所以这个动词可以想像任何被钉死、再无疑问的事：抓到嫌疑人、击中目标、找到答案。

intro.en: Nail is a Germanic word that has named both a hard plate on the body and a metal pin since Old English, and the two senses still share one form.
intro.cn: nail 是日耳曼语词，自古英语起就同时指身上的硬片和金属钉，这两个义项至今共用一个词形。

items.en: A reconstructed root for nail or claw is generally linked to this word, though the exact shape of the root is disputed.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词与一个表示「指甲、爪」的原始印欧语词根有关，但词根的具体形式仍有争议。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form naglaz named both the hard plate of a finger or toe and a metal peg.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 naglaz 同时指手指或脚趾的硬片与金属钉。

items.en: Old English nægl carried both meanings, so a finger nail and a board nail were the same word from the start.
items.cn: 古英语 nægl 兼具两义，所以手指甲和木板钉从一开始就是同一个词。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun and formed the verb nailen, meaning to fasten with a nail.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个名词，并造出动词 nailen，意为用钉子固定。

items.en: Modern English adds the informal sense of catching someone or getting something exactly right, as in nailing a suspect or an answer.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了口语义：抓住某人或把事情做得丝毫不差，如 nail a suspect、nail an answer。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely sound or look close to nail; the near-meaning group collects words for claws, pins and the act of fastening.
note.cn: 形近组收只是读音或拼写接近 nail 的词；近义组收表示爪、钉以及固定动作的词。

entries.definition: A small soft creature that moves slowly with a shell on its back; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 背壳、行动缓慢的小软体动物；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The small hollow in the middle of the stomach; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 腹部中间的凹陷，即肚脐；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The back of the neck; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 后颈；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The nail on a finger, formed from finger and nail.
entries.definitionCN: 手指上的指甲，由 finger 与 nail 复合而成。

entries.definition: A sharp curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟类或动物脚上弯曲而锋利的爪。

entries.definition: A short thin piece of metal used to hold things together.
entries.definitionCN: 用来把东西固定在一起的短细金属件。

entries.definition: To attach or fix something firmly in place.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定或连接在某处。

entries.definition: A small short nail with a wide head, used for cloth or paper.
entries.definitionCN: 钉布或纸用的、钉帽较宽的小短钉。

normalIntro.en: The word has been one shape for two jobs since Old English, and every sense grows out of something small and hard that holds.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词自古英语起就用一个词形承担两件事，每个义项都从「小而硬、能咬住」这个画面长出来。

normal.en: Old English nægl meant both finger nail and metal nail, so the two senses are twins rather than one borrowed from the other.
normal.cn: 古英语 nægl 同时指指甲和金属钉，两义是双胞胎，并非一个从另一个借来。

normal.en: Nailing a board is the verb built straight from the noun, which is why it needs no separate history.
normal.cn: 钉木板这个动词直接由名词构成，所以它没有另一段词源。

normal.en: Fingernail and toenail are compounds of finger or toe with nail, and each keeps the body sense.
normal.cn: fingernail 与 toenail 分别是 finger、toe 与 nail 的复合词，都保留了身体义。

normal.en: Hit the nail on the head pictures a hammer striking the exact spot, so the phrase means getting it exactly right.
normal.cn: 「hit the nail on the head」想像锤子正落在钉头上，所以这个说法指说得丝毫不差。

normal.en: Nail down adds down: the nail is driven fully home, so the details are fixed and no longer move.
normal.cn: nail down 加了 down：钉子被彻底钉到底，于是细节定死，不再变动。

abstract.en: A nail is a tiny thing that decides whether a heavy board stays put, which is why the word also means certainty.
abstract.cn: 钉子虽小，却决定一块重木板是否稳住，所以这个词也带有「确定」的意味。

abstract.en: Finger nail and metal nail share one word because both are a hard edge at the boundary of something softer.
abstract.cn: 指甲与铁钉共用一个词，因为两者都是较软之物边界上的一层硬边。

abstract.en: When police nail a suspect, the image is a case pinned down so that it can no longer shift.
abstract.cn: 警察 nail 住嫌疑人时，画面是一个案子被钉死，再也不能松动。

examples.en: He drove a nail into the loose board so that it would stop rattling.
examples.cn: 他把一枚钉子钉进松动的木板，好让它不再吱呀作响。

examples.en: She painted her nails a pale pink before the interview.
examples.cn: 面试前她把指甲涂成了淡粉色。

examples.en: The police nailed the driver at the second checkpoint.
examples.cn: 警方在第二个检查站逮住了那个司机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「耐哦」——钉子钉进去很耐，指甲也耐磨；记住 nail 是指甲、钉子，也是钉住。

root: 古英语 nægl（指甲；钉子），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 naglaz，更早或与原始印欧语表示「指甲、爪」的词根有关；同族词有 fingernail、toenail、nailbrush 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small hard plate or peg; the senses then divide into the body part, the metal tool, the act of using it, and the informal idea of pinning something down for certain.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一小片硬物或小钉；义项分出身体部位、金属工具、使用工具的动作，以及口语中「把某事钉死、再也无法狡辩」的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hammer drives a small hard pin into wood until only its flat head shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：锤子把小硬钉送进木板，最后只剩一个扁平的钉帽露在外面。

branches.en: a hand resting on a table, the tip of each finger capped in hard plate
branches.cn: 一只手搭在桌上，每个指尖都覆着一层硬片

branches.en: a row of clipped nails left on the edge of a basin
branches.cn: 脸盆边留下一排剪下的指甲

branches.en: one nail holding a heavy picture against a wall
branches.cn: 一枚钉子把沉重的画固定在墙上

branches.en: a hammer swinging down and a board going still
branches.cn: 锤子落下，木板随即不再晃动

branches.en: a case closed because the last doubt has been pinned down
branches.cn: 最后一个疑点被钉死，案子随之了结

intro.en: The entry is held together by one Old English noun, its English verb, and the compounds and endings built on it.
intro.cn: 这个词条由一个古英语名词、由它而来的英语动词，以及建在它上面的复合词与词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, and Latin has no noun that English used to build it, so no Latin cognate is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，拉丁语中没有英语用来构词的对应名词，所以这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: nail of a finger or toe, metal peg
hard plate or small metal pin

definition_zh: 裸体的；赤裸的；无遮盖的；不加掩饰的
definition_en: not wearing any clothes; not covered by the usual layer; or stated openly without disguise
core_image: 层层遮盖被一层层剥去，最后只剩没有任何外物包裹的身体
scene: 清晨的海滩上空无一人，几个孩子把衣服堆在沙丘边，光着脚往浪里跑。The boy ran naked into the cold water and came back laughing.
sceneCN: 这里是「裸体的、没穿衣服的」（第 1 个义项：身上没有任何衣物）；句意是男孩光着身子跑进冷水里，又笑着跑回来。图中可辨识物件：沙丘边的衣服、浅浪、光脚。

pos.zh: 裸体的；无遮盖的；不加掩饰的

derivatives.zh: 由 naked 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「赤裸；无遮盖」
由 naked 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「赤裸地；不加掩饰地」
由 naked 与 eye 复合而成，义为「肉眼观察的」

senses.title: Without any clothes on
senses.definition: not wearing any clothes, so that the whole body is open to view
senses.definitionCN: 没有穿任何衣物，整个身体都露在外面
senses.example: The child ran naked across the wet sand.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子光着身子跑过湿漉漉的沙滩。
senses.why: Old English nacod made a plain statement about the body: nothing is over the skin. That bare fact is the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nacod 只是对身体的直白陈述：皮肤上什么也没有盖。这个「什么都没有盖」的事实就是词的核心。

senses.title: Without the usual covering
senses.definition: not covered by the layer that normally protects or hides it, such as fur, leaves, paint or glass
senses.definitionCN: 缺少通常起保护或遮蔽作用的那一层，如毛、叶、漆或玻璃
senses.example: After the fire the hills stood naked in the morning light.
senses.exampleCN: 大火过后，山峦在晨光里光秃秃地立着。
senses.why: From a body without clothes the word moves to any surface missing its usual layer, because the picture is the same: a cover that ought to be there is gone.
senses.whyCN: 从没穿衣服的身体，这个词转到任何缺少惯常覆盖层的表面，画面其实一样：本该在那里的那层盖儿不见了。

senses.title: Open and undisguised
senses.definition: expressed or shown openly, with no attempt to hide it or make it softer
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达或显示出来，不做任何隐藏或软化
senses.example: He gave a naked account of how the money had disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫不掩饰地讲了那笔钱是怎么不见的。
senses.why: When nothing covers a body, nothing covers a fact either, so the word lends its image to truth, greed or aggression shown without a disguise.
senses.whyCN: 身体无物遮盖时，事实也一样无所遮盖，于是这个词把自己的画面借给了不加伪装地摆出来的真相、贪欲或侵略。

intro.en: Naked comes from a Germanic adjective for a bare body, and it has widened from clothes to any missing cover or disguise.
intro.cn: naked 源自日耳曼语中形容光裸身体的形容词，后来从衣物扩展到任何缺失的覆盖物或伪装。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning bare or unclothed is generally accepted, and it is also the distant source of Latin nudus.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「光裸、无衣」的原始印欧语词根，它也是拉丁语 nudus 的远源。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective nakwadaz meant naked or bare, without the sense of a covering that had been removed.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形容词 nakwadaz 意为光裸，并不含「被脱掉覆盖物」的意思。

items.en: Old English nacod described a body with nothing over it, and it could also describe bare ground or a bare fact.
items.cn: 古英语 nacod 描述身上无物遮盖的身体，也可以形容光秃的地面或赤裸的事实。

items.en: Middle English naked kept the same sense, and its -ed ending was already part of the word rather than a past participle.
items.cn: 中古英语的 naked 保持原义，词尾 -ed 早已是词本身的一部分，而不是过去分词标记。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for uncovered surfaces and undisguised statements, giving such phrases as naked eye, naked flame and the naked truth.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指无遮盖的表面与不加掩饰的说法，于是有 naked eye、naked flame、the naked truth 等表达。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the shape of a past participle ending in -ed but have no link in origin; the near-meaning group collects words for a body or surface with nothing on it.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带 -ed 结尾、外形相像但词源无关的词；近义组收表示身体或表面无物遮盖的词。

entries.definition: Cooked by dry heat in an oven; only the ending looks alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 在炉中用干热烤熟的；只是词尾外形相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Made to look real when it is not; only the ending looks alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 把假的东西做得像真的；只是词尾外形相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Morally bad, or playfully mischievous; the -ed is pronounced the same way, but the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 道德上坏的，或淘气顽皮的；其中 -ed 读音相同，但词源不同。

entries.definition: Not covered by clothes or by the usual layer.
entries.definitionCN: 没有衣物或惯常覆盖层的。

entries.definition: Not wearing clothes, especially in art or a formal description.
entries.definitionCN: 未穿衣服的，尤用于艺术或正式描述。

entries.definition: Left open to view or to harm, with no protection.
entries.definitionCN: 暴露在视线或伤害之下的，没有防护的。

entries.definition: Not wearing clothes; a formal word for the same plain fact.
entries.definitionCN: 没穿衣服的；同一个朴素事实的正式说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective for a bare body, and the -ed at the end is part of its history rather than a grammar ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中形容光裸身体的形容词，末尾的 -ed 属于它的历史，而不是语法词尾。

normal.en: Old English nacod is the direct ancestor, and the modern form keeps the same three consonants after the vowels shifted.
normal.cn: 古英语 nacod 是直接祖先，元音变化之后现代词形仍保留同样的三个辅音。

normal.en: The -ed is not a past tense ending: it has been inside the word since Old English, so naked does not mean having been naked.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ed 不是过去式词尾：它自古英语就在词里，所以 naked 并不表示「曾经裸过」。

normal.en: Naked eye means the eye with no lens or glass in front of it, which is the missing-cover sense at work.
normal.cn: naked eye 指前面没有镜片或玻璃的眼睛，正是「缺少覆盖层」这一义在起作用。

normal.en: Naked flame means fire with nothing around it, the same idea of a bare surface with no protection.
normal.cn: naked flame 指周围没有任何遮挡的火，同样是「裸露无防护」的意思。

normal.en: Nudus is the Latin word for bare, and it is a distant cousin of naked rather than the word that gave it birth.
normal.cn: nudus 是拉丁语中表示光裸的词，它是 naked 的远亲，而不是生出 naked 的母词。

abstract.en: Picture a body with every layer peeled away, and you have the single picture behind clothes, hills and truth.
abstract.cn: 想像一具被一层层剥去遮盖的身体，你就得到了贯穿衣物、山峦与真相的那一个画面。

abstract.en: A cover can be cloth, fur, paint or polite wording; the word treats all of them as the same thing when they are gone.
abstract.cn: 遮盖可以是布、毛、漆或客气的措辞；这个词把它们消失时的情形都看成同一件事。

abstract.en: Calling a fact naked says that no acceptable wording stands between the listener and the thing itself.
abstract.cn: 把一件事实称作 naked，等于说听者与事情本身之间没有任何可接受的措辞挡着。

examples.en: The child ran naked across the wet sand.
examples.cn: 那孩子光着身子跑过湿漉漉的沙滩。

examples.en: The planet is too faint to see with the naked eye.
examples.cn: 那颗行星太暗，用肉眼看不见。

examples.en: He gave a naked account of what had gone wrong.
examples.cn: 他毫不掩饰地讲了事情是怎么出错的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内壳的」——把外壳整个脱掉，露出里面；记住 naked 是赤裸的、无遮盖的。

root: 古英语 nacod（光裸的），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 nakwadaz，更早可追溯到原始印欧语表示「光裸」的词根，与拉丁语 nudus 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body with nothing over the skin; the senses then extend that missing cover to surfaces and to facts stated without disguise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是皮肤上无物遮盖的身体；义项再把「缺少覆盖」扩展到表面，以及不加掩饰地说出的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: layer after layer of covering is stripped away until the body itself is all that remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层层遮盖被剥掉，最后只剩下身体本身。

branches.en: a child running into the sea with nothing on
branches.cn: 孩子身上什么也没穿，径直跑进海里

branches.en: a towel left on the sand beside a pile of clothes
branches.cn: 沙地上一条毛巾搁在一堆衣服旁

branches.en: hills stripped of grass after a fire
branches.cn: 大火之后被剥去草皮的山

branches.en: a wall with its paint gone, showing the bare brick
branches.cn: 墙面掉了漆，露出光秃秃的砖

branches.en: a sentence that hides nothing and softens nothing
branches.cn: 一句既不遮掩也不软化的话

intro.en: One Old English adjective, its English endings and compounds, and a Latin cousin that is related but not its source hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语形容词、由它而来的英语词尾与复合词，以及一个相关但并非其来源的拉丁远亲，共同撑起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin nudus and its verb nudare are generally treated as distant cognates of naked, related through the same older root rather than borrowed from each other.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nudus 及其动词 nudare 一般认为与 naked 同源，通过同一个更古老的词根相关联，而不是彼此借入。

items.meaning: adjective ending, not a past tense here
items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾，此处并非过去式

definition_zh: 名字；名称；名声；命名；任命
definition_en: the word by which a person or thing is known; the reputation attached to that word; and, as a verb, to give such a word or to appoint someone
core_image: 一块木牌上刻着一个字，牌子挂上去，这件东西就有了被人呼唤的身份
scene: 村口的老槐树下，几位老人翻着泛黄的族谱，为新添的孩子挑一个合适的字。They named the baby after her grandmother, and the whole family agreed.
sceneCN: 这里是「命名、给……取名」（第 3 个义项：为某人或某物取名字）；句意是他们照着祖母的名字给宝宝取名，全家人都赞成。图中可辨识物件：族谱、老槐树、写字的木牌。

derivatives.zh: 由 name 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无名的；不知名的」
由 name 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「即；也就是」
由 name 与 plate 复合而成，义为「名牌」
由前缀 re-（重新）与 name 复合而成，义为「重新命名」

senses.title: The word by which a person or thing is known
senses.definition: the word or set of words used to identify a person, animal, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用来指认某人、某动物、某地或某物的词或词组
senses.example: She wrote her name at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她把名字写在了页面顶端。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the spoken label that calls a person over; every other sense in the word grows out of that act of naming.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是喊人时用的那个称呼；这个词的其他义项都从「叫名字」这个动作长出来。

senses.title: The reputation attached to a person or group
senses.definition: the opinion that other people have of a person, company or product, built up over time
senses.definitionCN: 他人对某人、某公司或某产品长期形成的看法
senses.example: The old bakery still has a good name in this neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老面包店在这一带仍然名声很好。
senses.why: A name stands for a person, so it can also stand for how that person is judged; the label becomes the reputation hanging on it.
senses.whyCN: 名字代表一个人，因此也能代表别人对他的评价；这个标签就变成了挂在它上面的名声。

senses.title: To give a name to someone or something
senses.definition: to give a name to a person, animal, place or thing, especially at the start of its life or use
senses.definitionCN: 给某人、某动物、某地或某物取名字，尤指在生命或使用的开端
senses.example: They named the boat after the captain's daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以船长的女儿为这条船命名。
senses.why: The noun supplies the label and the verb supplies the act of putting that label on a new thing, so a baby, a boat and a street can all be named.
senses.whyCN: 名词提供标签，动词提供「把标签贴到新事物上」的动作，所以婴儿、船只和街道都可以被命名。

senses.title: To appoint or specify someone
senses.definition: to officially choose someone for a position, or to state exactly which person or thing is meant
senses.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某职，或明确指出所指的是哪个人或哪件东西
senses.example: The board named her as the new director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会任命她为新任主管。
senses.why: A name singles one person out of a crowd, so the verb can mean picking that person and putting them into a post, with the authority of the speaker behind it.
senses.whyCN: 名字把一个人从人群里单独点出来，所以这个动词可以指把那个人挑出来放到某个职位上，背后是说话者的权力在起作用。

intro.en: Name goes back to an old word for the spoken label, and its senses have spread from that label to reputation and to the act of appointing.
intro.cn: name 可追溯到表示「口头称呼」的古词，义项从这一称呼扩展到名声，再扩展到任命这一动作。

items.en: A reconstructed noun for name is widely accepted, and the same root lies behind Latin nomen and Greek onoma.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「名字」的原始印欧语名词，同一个词根也见于拉丁语 nomen 与希腊语 onoma。

items.en: The reconstructed form namô meant name, and it is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.cn: 重构形式 namô 意为名字，是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.en: Old English nama was the everyday noun for a name, and it also supplied the verb namian, to name.
items.cn: 古英语 nama 是表示名字的日常名词，并派生出动词 namian，意为命名。

items.en: Middle English kept name as a noun and namen as a verb, and the spelling settled into its modern shape.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词 name 与动词 namen，拼写逐渐固定为现代形式。

items.en: Modern English extends the noun to reputation and the verb to official appointment, as in naming a new director.
items.cn: 现代英语把名词扩展到名声，把动词扩展到正式任命，如 naming a new director。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the word's own family and a few spellings that merely rhyme; the near-meaning group collects words for labels, titles and reputation.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及几个只是押韵的拼写；近义组收表示标签、头衔与名声的词。

entries.definition: An adverb built from name and -ly, used to introduce an exact term.
entries.definitionCN: 由 name 加 -ly 构成的副词，用来引出确切的词语。

entries.definition: Having no name, or too ordinary or bad to be described by one.
entries.definitionCN: 没有名字的，或平凡、恶劣得无法用名字描述的。

entries.definition: Existing in name only, or relating to a name; from the Latin nomen.
entries.definitionCN: 仅名义上存在的，或与名字有关的；出自拉丁语 nomen。

entries.definition: The state of being known by many people; it rhymes with name but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 被很多人知晓的状态；与 name 押韵，但词源不同。

entries.definition: The word attached to a book, film or person as a mark of rank.
entries.definitionCN: 附在书籍、影片或人身上、表示等级或名称的词。

entries.definition: A small piece of paper or a short word that says what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 说明某物是什么的小纸片或简短词语。

entries.definition: The general belief that people hold about someone's character or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 人们对某人品格或品质普遍持有的看法。

entries.definition: To choose someone officially for a purpose or post.
entries.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某职或用于某目的。

normalIntro.en: The word is the plain noun for a spoken label, and all its senses are different ways of using that label.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是表示「口头称呼」的朴素名词，所有义项都是使用这一称呼的不同方式。

normal.en: Old English nama is the direct ancestor, and the modern spelling keeps the same four letters at the start.
normal.cn: 古英语 nama 是直接祖先，现代拼写开头仍保留同样的四个字母。

normal.en: Namely is name plus -ly, and it introduces the exact name of the thing just mentioned.
normal.cn: namely 是 name 加 -ly，用来引出前面那件事的确切名字。

normal.en: Nameless is name plus -less, so it describes someone with no name or no distinct identity.
normal.cn: nameless 是 name 加 -less，用来形容没有名字或没有鲜明身份的人。

normal.en: Nomen is the Latin word for name, and it gives English nominal, nominate and nomination.
normal.cn: nomen 是拉丁语中的「名字」，由此有了英语的 nominal、nominate、nomination。

normal.en: In the name of is a fixed phrase in which name stands for the authority behind an act.
normal.cn: in the name of 是固定说法，这里的 name 代表一个行为背后的权力。

abstract.en: A name is a sound that makes one thing stand out from everything else, so the word is always about singling out.
abstract.cn: 名字是一种让某物从其他一切中站出来的声音，所以这个词始终关乎「单独点出」。

abstract.en: Because a name travels without the person, it can carry praise or blame long after the person is gone.
abstract.cn: 名字可以脱离本人四处流传，所以人不在场之后，它仍能承载赞誉或责备。

abstract.en: To be named to a post is to be pointed at in public, which is why the verb can mean both calling and choosing.
abstract.cn: 被任命到一个职位，就是在众人面前被点到，所以这个动词既能指称呼，也能指挑选。

examples.en: She wrote her name at the top of the page.
examples.cn: 她把名字写在了页面顶端。

examples.en: They named the boat after the captain's daughter.
examples.cn: 他们以船长的女儿为这条船命名。

examples.en: The old bakery still has a good name in this neighbourhood.
examples.cn: 那家老面包店在这一带仍然名声很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内姆」——先记住对方的名字，才好开口叫；记住 name 是名字，也是命名。

root: 古英语 nama（名字），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 namô，更早与原始印欧语表示「名字」的词根有关；同族词有 namely、nameless、nameplate、rename 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a spoken label; the senses then divide into the label itself, the reputation it carries, the act of giving it, and the act of pointing to a chosen person.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个口头称呼；义项分出称呼本身、它承载的名声、给它命名的动作，以及把选定之人点出来的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden board is carved with one word and hung up, and from then on the thing has an identity people can call.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木牌刻上一个字、挂了起来，从此这件东西就有了可被人呼唤的身份。

branches.en: a child learning to write the letters of her own name
branches.cn: 孩子学着写下自己名字的字母

branches.en: a wooden board above a shop door with one word carved into it
branches.cn: 店门上方一块木牌上刻着一个词

branches.en: a family bakery whose sign is trusted across the district
branches.cn: 一块被整个街区信赖的老面包店招牌

branches.en: a boat taking the name of someone loved
branches.cn: 一条船得到了心爱之人的名字

branches.en: a hand raised in a meeting to point at one person
branches.cn: 会上举起手，指向某一个人

intro.en: One Old English noun, its English verb and suffixes, and a Latin family with the same older root hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语名词、由它而来的英语动词与后缀，以及共享同一古老词根的拉丁词族，共同撑起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen is generally treated as a cognate of name through the same older root, and it is the source of the learned words nominal and nominate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nomen 一般认为通过同一古老词根与 name 同源，并且是书面词 nominal、nominate 的来源。

to give a name, to appoint

definition_zh: 即；也就是；具体地说
definition_en: used to introduce a more exact statement or a list of specific items that explains what has just been said
core_image: 说话人停了一下，把手指点在刚说过的那个笼统词上，补出它确切的名字
scene: 会议散场后，两个同事在走廊里压低声音核对证书上的措辞，其中一人伸手指了指纸上的最后一行。Only one name can go on the certificate, namely the person who took the course.
sceneCN: 这里是「即、也就是」（第 1 个义项：把前面的话说得更具体）；句意是证书上只能写一个名字，也就是上过这门课的那个人。图中可辨识物件：证书、走廊、手指着的那一行字。

collocations.zh: 即……（后接从句，把前面的话说具体）

derivatives.zh: namely 的基础词，义为「名字」；副词由它加 -ly 构成
由 name 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无名的」
由前缀 re-（重新）与 name 复合而成，义为「重新命名」

senses.title: Introducing a more precise statement
senses.titleCN: 即；也就是（把话说得更具体）
senses.definition: used after a comma to introduce a more exact statement about the thing just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用在逗号之后，引出对刚才所提事物更精确的说法
senses.example: Only one person can sign the contract, namely the owner.
senses.exampleCN: 合同只能由一个人签，也就是业主本人。
senses.why: Namely is name turned into an adverb, so its work is to put the exact name on something the speaker has just left vague.
senses.whyCN: namely 是 name 加后缀变成的副词，它的任务就是给说话人刚说得笼统的东西补上确切的名字。

senses.title: Introducing a list of specific items
senses.titleCN: 即；也就是（列举具体项目）
senses.definition: used after a comma to introduce the particular items that make up a group just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用在逗号之后，引出构成刚才所说整体的具体项目
senses.example: Two countries signed the treaty, namely France and Spain.
senses.exampleCN: 两个国家签署了这项条约，即法国和西班牙。
senses.why: When several names follow one another, the same act of naming becomes an enumeration, which is why the word can introduce a list as well as a single term.
senses.whyCN: 当几个名字接连出现，同一个「点名」的动作就变成了逐项列举，所以这个词既能引出一个名称，也能引出一串项目。

intro.en: Namely is an English adverb built from the noun name, and the adverbial ending that formed it has been in the language since Old English.
intro.cn: namely 是由名词 name 构成的英语副词，构成它的副词词尾自古英语就存在。

items.en: The reconstructed noun for name is the starting point; the adverb is a much later English construction on that base.
items.cn: 起点是重构的表示「名字」的名词；这个副词是在这一基础上很久之后才由英语造出的。

items.en: The reconstructed form namô kept the noun sense of name and passed it into Old English as nama.
items.cn: 重构形式 namô 保留了「名字」的名词义，并以 nama 的形式传入古英语。

items.en: Old English had nama as the noun and the adverb-forming suffix -lice, which could attach to nouns to make adverbs of manner.
items.cn: 古英语有名词 nama，也有构成副词的词尾 -lice，它可以加在名词后构成方式副词。

items.en: Middle English shortened -lice to -li, and name plus -li produced the adverb namely, first used in the sense of by name.
items.cn: 中古英语把 -lice 缩短为 -li，name 加 -li 就造出了副词 namely，最早表示「按名字、指名地」。

items.en: Modern English narrowed the meaning to that is to say, so the word now introduces an exact term or a list rather than naming a person directly.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义收窄为「也就是说」，于是这个词现在引出确切的词语或一串项目，而不再直接给某人点名。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and the words built on the same base; the near-meaning group collects phrases that restate something more exactly.
note.cn: 形近组收那个名词以及建在同一基础上的词；近义组收把前文说得更确切的说法。

entries.definition: The noun from which the adverb is built, meaning the word by which something is known.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个副词的名词，义为「名字」。

entries.definition: Without a name, or too ordinary or bad to be given one.
entries.definitionCN: 没有名字的，或平凡、恶劣得无法命名的。

entries.definition: In name only, or according to what is officially stated; from Latin nomen.
entries.definitionCN: 名义上的，或按官方说法；出自拉丁语 nomen。

entries.definition: To give a new or different name to something.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物取新的或不同的名字。

entries.definition: A phrase used to introduce a clearer version of what was just said.
entries.definitionCN: 用来引出对刚才所说内容的更清楚版本。

entries.definition: A longer phrase with the same job of restating something more exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 一个更长的说法，作用相同，都是把前文更确切地重说一遍。

entries.definition: In a way that names the exact thing rather than a general class.
entries.definitionCN: 点明确切事物而不是笼统类别的说法。

entries.definition: A phrase that repeats an idea in a different and usually simpler form.
entries.definitionCN: 用另一种、通常更简单的说法重复同一个意思。

normalIntro.en: The word is a noun turned adverb, and its one job is to replace a vague phrase with an exact name or a list of names.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是由名词变成的副词，唯一的任务就是用确切的名字或一串名字替换笼统的说法。

normal.en: Namely is name plus -ly, so the adverb literally carries the noun's job of naming.
normal.cn: namely 是 name 加 -ly，所以这个副词本身就带着名词「命名」的职责。

normal.en: The modern -ly comes from Old English -lice, which is why the ending looks like the ending of other manner adverbs.
normal.cn: 现代的 -ly 来自古英语 -lice，所以这个词尾看起来和其他方式副词一样。

normal.en: Namely sits after a comma and before the exact term, and it never begins a sentence on its own.
normal.cn: namely 站在逗号之后、确切词语之前，从不单独起句。

normal.en: Namely introduces a noun phrase or a list rather than a full clause, so a whole sentence after it is usually wrong.
normal.cn: namely 引出的是名词短语或一串项目，而不是完整从句，所以后面接整句通常是错的。

normal.en: The older sense was by name, which shows that the word began as a way of pointing at a person directly.
normal.cn: 较早的义项是「按名字、指名地」，说明这个词最初是直接指向某个人的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker pausing, then putting a finger on the vague word and writing the real name under it.
abstract.cn: 想像说话人停顿一下，把手指按在笼统的词上，在它下面写出真正的名字。

abstract.en: A list after namely is not extra information; it is the unpacking of a single word that was too broad.
abstract.cn: namely 后面的清单不是补充信息，而是把一个过于宽泛的词拆开摆出来。

abstract.en: The word is exactness itself, which is why it sounds stiff in speech and natural in definitions and contracts.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是「精确」本身，所以它在口语里显得生硬，在定义和合同里却很自然。

examples.en: Only one person can sign the contract, namely the owner.
examples.cn: 合同只能由一个人签，也就是业主本人。

examples.en: Two countries signed the treaty, namely France and Spain.
examples.cn: 两个国家签署了这项条约，即法国和西班牙。

examples.en: He gave two reasons, namely cost and time.
examples.cn: 他给了两个理由，即成本和时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内姆里」——把话里那个笼统的说法点出名字来；记住 namely 是即、也就是。

root: 由 name（名字）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，-ly 源自古英语副词词尾 -lice，最初表示「按名字、指名地」，后收窄为「也就是说」。

sensesIntro.en: There are two uses rather than many senses: one points at a single exact term, the other unpacks a group into its named parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词只有两种用法而不是许多义项：一种指出单个确切词语，另一种把整体拆成一个个点名的部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker pauses and places a finger on a vague word, then writes the exact name beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：说话人停顿下来，把手指按在一个笼统的词上，然后在下面写出确切的名字。

branches.cn: 一只手点着证书上的某一行

branches.en: a vague promise replaced by one exact name
branches.cn: 一句笼统的承诺被一个确切的名字替换

branches.en: two names read out one after the other
branches.cn: 两个名字被依次念出来

branches.en: a short list standing where a group word used to be
branches.cn: 一串短名单取代了原来的笼统说法

branches.en: a comma followed by the words that make a statement precise
branches.cn: 逗号之后跟着几个让陈述变确切的词

intro.en: The entry rests on the noun name, the two adverbial endings that formed the word, and the Latin family behind the noun.
intro.cn: 这个词条依托名词 name、构成它的两个副词词尾，以及名词背后的拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen is a cognate of the English noun name rather than the source of the adverb, and it stands behind the learned word nominally.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nomen 是英语名词 name 的同源词，而不是这个副词的来源，它是书面词 nominally 的基础。

definition_zh: 狭窄的；狭隘的；勉强的；变窄
definition_en: measuring a small distance from side to side; limited in range or outlook; won or avoided by only a small margin; and, as a verb, to become less wide
core_image: 两堵墙向中间挤过来，人只能侧着身子从缝隙里通过
scene: 老城的巷子两边砌着高墙，一辆送货车停在巷口，司机探头量了量两侧后视镜。The lane was too narrow for the van, so the driver backed out slowly.
sceneCN: 这里是「狭窄的」（第 1 个义项：两侧之间距离小）；句意是这条巷子太窄，货车过不去，司机只好慢慢倒车出来。图中可辨识物件：高墙、后视镜、巷口的货车。

derivatives.zh: 由 narrow 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「勉强地；差一点」
由 narrow 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「狭窄；狭隘」
由 narrow 与 minded 复合而成，义为「心胸狭隘的」

senses.title: Small in width
senses.definition: measuring only a small distance from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从一侧到另一侧的距离很小
senses.example: The alley is too narrow for a truck to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这条小巷太窄，卡车过不去。
senses.why: Old English nearu described a space with little room across, and that plain physical tightness is the centre of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nearu 描述横向余量很小的空间，这种朴素的物理上的「挤」是后来所有义项的核心。

senses.title: Limited in scope or outlook
senses.definition: limited in range, sympathy or understanding, and not open to other views
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、同情心或理解力上受限，不愿接纳别的看法
senses.example: The debate was framed by a narrow set of questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论被一组狭窄的问题限制住了。
senses.why: A space with little room across becomes a mind with little room for other ideas, so the physical tightness turns into a limit on thought.
senses.whyCN: 横向余量很小的空间，会变成容不下别的想法的心胸，于是物理上的「挤」就转成了对思想的限制。

senses.title: Barely achieved or barely avoided
senses.definition: achieved by only a small margin, or avoided by only a little distance or time
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的差距取得，或只差一点就避开的
senses.example: She won the vote by a narrow margin of two votes.
senses.exampleCN: 她以两票的微弱优势赢得了表决。
senses.why: When the gap between two outcomes is narrow, the winner passes with almost no room to spare, so the word marks a close result or escape.
senses.whyCN: 当两种结果的间隙很窄时，赢的一方几乎没有余量地挤过去，所以这个词用来标记接近的结果或险境。

senses.title: To become or make less wide
senses.definition: to become less wide, or to reduce the width or range of something
senses.definitionCN: 变得不那么宽，或把某物的宽度、范围缩小
senses.example: The road narrows sharply after the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 过了桥之后，路突然变窄。
senses.why: If the adjective names a small width, the verb names the movement toward it: the two sides come closer and the space shrinks.
senses.whyCN: 如果形容词指的是小宽度，动词指的就是朝这个宽度靠拢的过程：两侧靠近，空间缩小。

intro.en: Narrow is a Germanic adjective for tight space, and the deeper root is uncertain; its senses have spread from width to scope and to a close margin.
intro.cn: narrow 是日耳曼语中形容逼仄空间的形容词，更早的词根不确定；义项从宽度扩展到范围，再扩展到微小的差距。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain, and no single reconstructed root for this Germanic adjective is agreed on.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定，学界并未就这个词的原始印欧语词根达成一致。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective narwaz meant narrow or tight, and it is the generally accepted starting point.
items.cn: 一般认为重构的形容词 narwaz 意为狭窄、逼仄，这是普遍接受的起点。

items.en: Old English nearu meant narrow and confined, and it could also name distress or oppression, the feeling of being squeezed.
items.cn: 古英语 nearu 意为狭窄、受拘束，也可指困苦或压迫，也就是被挤住的感觉。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as narwe or narow, and its meaning settled on small width in space.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词写作 narwe 或 narow，词义固定为空间上的宽度小。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective to limited scope and close margins, and forms the verb narrow, with the phrase narrow down.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词扩展到有限的范围与微小的差距，并造出动词 narrow，以及短语 narrow down。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that end in the same -ow sound but have no shared origin; the near-meaning group collects words for tight space and limited range.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 -ow 音结尾、但并无共同来源的词；近义组收表示逼仄空间与有限范围的词。

entries.definition: A thin pointed stick shot from a bow; only the ending sounds alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 从弓上射出的细尖木杆，即箭；只是词尾读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The soft substance inside bones; only the ending sounds alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 骨头内部的柔软物质，即骨髓；只是词尾读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A heavy farm tool that breaks up soil; only the ending sounds alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 打碎土块的沉重农具，即耙；只是词尾读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small brown bird common in towns; only the ending sounds alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇常见的小型褐色鸟，即麻雀；只是词尾读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Fitting closely, with little space to spare.
entries.definitionCN: 空间几乎不留余量的、紧绷的。

entries.definition: Too small and crowded for comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 狭小拥挤、让人不舒服的。

entries.definition: Kept within limits, not allowed to spread.
entries.definitionCN: 被限制在范围内、不许扩张的。

entries.definition: Small in amount or range, with a fixed boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或范围小、有固定边界的。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from tight space, and its later senses are that tightness applied to thought, to results and to movement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从逼仄的空间起步，后面的义项都是把这种「挤」用到想法、结果和动作上。

normal.en: Old English nearu meant both narrow and oppressed, which shows that tight space and tight feeling were one idea.
normal.cn: 古英语 nearu 既指狭窄也指受压迫，说明空间的挤与感受上的压抑本是同一个概念。

normal.en: Narrow-minded is narrow plus minded, so a small room in the head stands for a small range of ideas.
normal.cn: narrow-minded 是 narrow 加 minded，脑子里的小房间就成了狭窄的想法范围。

normal.en: Narrow escape keeps the picture of passing through a gap with almost no room on either side.
normal.cn: narrow escape 保留了从两侧几乎无余量的缝隙中穿过的画面。

normal.en: Narrow down adds down: the range is pushed smaller and smaller until only one thing is left.
normal.cn: narrow down 加了 down：范围被越压越小，最后只剩一样东西。

normal.en: The verb narrow is simply the adjective put into motion, so it means the sides moving closer together.
normal.cn: 动词 narrow 就是把形容词变成动作，意思是两侧互相靠近。

abstract.en: A narrow street and a narrow mind share one picture: too little room for anything else to pass.
abstract.cn: 狭窄的街道与狭隘的心胸共用一个画面：几乎没有余量让别的东西通过。

abstract.en: A narrow victory is not a small victory but one that barely fitted through the gap.
abstract.cn: 险胜并不是小胜，而是勉强从缝隙里挤过去的一次胜利。

abstract.en: Every sense measures the distance between two edges, whether those edges are walls, ideas or vote counts.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在量两条边之间的距离，无论那两条边是墙、想法还是票数。

examples.en: The lane was too narrow for the van, so the driver backed out slowly.
examples.cn: 这条巷子太窄，货车过不去，司机只好慢慢倒车出来。

examples.en: She won the vote by a narrow margin of two votes.
examples.cn: 她以两票的微弱优势赢得了表决。

examples.en: The path narrows as it climbs towards the ridge.
examples.cn: 小路向山脊爬升时越来越窄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捏肉」——两堵墙往中间捏，把肉都挤住了；记住 narrow 是狭窄的、变窄。

root: 古英语 nearu（狭窄的、受拘束的，也可指困苦），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 narwaz；更早的词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small distance between two sides; the senses then apply it to range of thought, to the margin of a result, and to the act of shrinking.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两侧之间很小的距离；义项再把它用到思想的范围、结果的差距，以及收缩这个动作上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls press inward until a person can only pass sideways through the gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堵墙向中间挤压，人只能侧着身子从缝隙里通过。

branches.en: two high walls leaving one narrow lane
branches.cn: 两堵高墙之间只留一条窄巷

branches.en: a van stopping at the mouth of an alley it cannot enter
branches.cn: 货车停在巷口，进不去

branches.en: a list of questions too short to cover the whole problem
branches.cn: 一组问题太窄，盖不住整个问题

branches.en: a vote decided by two ballots out of hundreds
branches.cn: 几百张票里靠两张定输赢

branches.en: a road pinching together as it climbs
branches.cn: 道路向上延伸时逐渐收窄

intro.en: The entry is held together by the Old English adjective, its English verb, and the endings and compounds built on the same short base.
intro.cn: 这个词条由古英语形容词、由它而来的英语动词，以及建在同一词基上的词尾与复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and its deeper root is uncertain, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded and none is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，更早的词根不确定，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，所以这里不列。

definition_zh: 令人厌恶的；恶劣的；下流的
definition_en: very unpleasant to the senses; severe or dangerous; and morally dirty or spiteful
core_image: 一块黏糊糊的霉斑，让人下意识缩回手
scene: 厨房角落的剩菜已经长出霉点，酸味冲得人直往后退。The milk at the back of the fridge had turned nasty.
sceneCN: 这里 nasty 是「令人厌恶的」（第 1 个义项：气味或外表使人反感）；句意为冰箱深处的牛奶已经变质发臭。图中可辨识物件：发霉的剩菜、冰箱隔层。

pos.zh: 令人厌恶的；恶劣的；下流的

derivatives.zh: 由 nasty 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「厌恶；下流」
由 nasty 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「令人厌恶地；恶意地」

senses.title: Very unpleasant to the senses
senses.titleCN: 令人厌恶的；难闻难看的
senses.definition: so unpleasant to see, smell, taste or touch that a person wants to move away from it
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉、气味、味道或触感上让人反感，使人想躲开
senses.example: A nasty smell came from the rubbish bin.
senses.exampleCN: 垃圾桶里传来一股难闻的味道。
senses.why: The earliest record of the word described something filthy, so the sense starts from physical dirt that the senses reject.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的记录指肮脏的东西，所以词义起点是感官排斥的身体污秽。

senses.title: Severe, dangerous or hard to deal with
senses.titleCN: 恶劣的；严重的；难对付的
senses.definition: used of weather, injuries, problems or events that are severe and cause real trouble
senses.definitionCN: 用于天气、伤势、问题或事件，表示严重并带来实际麻烦
senses.example: He took a nasty fall on the icy steps.
senses.exampleCN: 他在结冰的台阶上摔了很重的一跤。
senses.why: Once the word means bad to the senses, English stretches it from what smells wrong to what goes wrong, so an injury or a storm can be nasty.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「感官上不好」扩展到「事情出岔子」，受伤或风暴这类带来麻烦的事也就成了 nasty。

senses.title: Spiteful or morally dirty
senses.definition: used of words, jokes or people that are unkind, spiteful or sexually coarse
senses.definitionCN: 用于言语、玩笑或人，表示刻薄、怀有恶意或色情粗俗
senses.example: She spread nasty rumours about her rival.
senses.exampleCN: 她散布关于对手的恶意谣言。
senses.why: Filth moves easily from the body to behaviour: a dirty mouth or a dirty trick carries the same disgust that a dirty smell does.
senses.whyCN: 「脏」很容易从身体转到行为上：一张脏嘴或一个脏手段，带来的厌恶和闻到脏东西时一样。

intro.en: The word is first recorded in Middle English as nasti, and its earlier source is disputed, so the account below marks the uncertain links.
intro.cn: 这个词最早以 nasti 的形式见于中古英语，更早的来源有争议，因此下面的叙述会标明不确定的环节。

items.en: Nasti is recorded in the fourteenth century with the sense of dirty and filthy.
items.cn: 十四世纪的文献里出现 nasti，意为肮脏的、污秽的。

items.en: One common suggestion traces it to an Old French form such as nastre, meaning filthy, but the record is thin.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它追溯到意为「肮脏」的古法语形式 nastre，但证据很薄弱。

items.en: Another suggestion links it to Dutch nestig, literally nest-like, that is, dirty as a nest.
items.cn: 另一种说法把它联系到荷兰语 nestig，字面是「像鸟窝的」，即像窝一样脏。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word covers not only filth but also coarse speech and spiteful behaviour.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词不只指污秽，还指粗俗的言语和恶意的行为。

items.en: Modern English keeps the informal force of the word and uses it freely for bad weather, bad injuries and bad problems.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这个词的口语力度，广泛用于恶劣天气、严重伤势和棘手问题。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same stem; the near-meaning group collects words for disgust and unpleasantness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形式；近义组收表示厌恶与不快之感的词。

entries.definition: The noun made from nasty with -ness, meaning the quality of being nasty.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nasty 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「厌恶；下流」。

entries.definition: The adverb made from nasty with -ly, meaning in a nasty way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nasty 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「令人厌恶地；恶意地」。

entries.definition: A garden plant with bright flowers; its Latin name means nose-twister and only looks like nasty.
entries.definitionCN: 一种开亮色花的园艺植物；其拉丁名意为「扭鼻子」，只是拼写与 nasty 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: So unpleasant that it makes a person feel sick.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反胃的；极讨厌的。

entries.definition: Dirty, unpleasant and often smelling bad.
entries.definitionCN: 肮脏的；难闻的。

entries.definition: Not enjoyable or comfortable to experience.
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快的；不舒服的。

normalIntro.en: The word has a disputed stem and three productive English endings, which together cover the adjective, the noun and the adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词有一个来源有争议的词干和三个能产的英语词尾，分别撑起形容词、名词和副词。

normal.en: Nasti in Middle English already meant filthy, so the disgust sense is the oldest one.
normal.cn: 中古英语里的 nasti 已经表示污秽，所以「厌恶」是最老的义项。

normal.en: Nastiness and nastily are built with plain suffixes, so the family is small and easy to keep straight.
normal.cn: nastiness 与 nastily 都由普通后缀构成，词族很小，好记不乱。

normal.en: A nasty fall and nasty weather keep the same idea: something bad has happened to you.
normal.cn: nasty fall 与 nasty weather 保留同一个想法：有坏事落到你头上。

normal.en: Nasty words are called dirty words because English reuses the language of filth for meanness.
normal.cn: 恶毒的话被叫作「脏话」，因为英语把污秽的说法挪去形容刻薄。

normal.en: The comparative is nastier, not more nasty, so the ending behaves like happy and pretty.
normal.cn: 比较级是 nastier，而不是 more nasty，词尾变化和 happy、pretty 一样。

abstract.en: A word that begins with a smell and ends with a rumour shows how one kind of disgust can spread to another.
abstract.cn: 一个词从气味开始、到谣言结束，说明一种厌恶如何蔓延到另一种。

abstract.en: Nasty is English at its most physical: the nose learns the word before the mind does.
abstract.cn: nasty 是英语里最身体化的词之一：鼻子比脑子先学会它。

abstract.en: Saying that a problem is nasty quietly admits that it may beat you.
abstract.cn: 说一个问题 nasty，其实是在悄悄承认它可能把你难倒。

examples.en: The fridge had a nasty smell after the power cut.
examples.cn: 断电之后冰箱里有一股难闻的味道。

examples.en: He took a nasty fall while running down the stairs.
examples.cn: 他跑下楼梯时重重摔了一跤。

examples.en: Her nasty remarks spoiled the whole evening.
examples.cn: 她那几句恶毒的话毁了整个晚上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那个死地」——一提到那个地方就嫌恶地皱眉；记住 nasty 是令人厌恶的。

root: 中古英语 nasti（肮脏的、污秽的），来源不确定，一般认为与古法语 nastre 或荷兰语 nestig 有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is sensory disgust; from it the word reaches severe trouble and then dirty behaviour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是感官上的厌恶；由此延伸到严重的麻烦，再伸向下流的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sticky patch of mould that makes the hand pull back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黏糊糊的霉斑，让人下意识缩回手。

branches.en: a bin overflowing beside a warm kitchen door
branches.cn: 温热的厨房门边堆满溢出的垃圾

branches.en: a child holding its nose at a plate of spoiled food
branches.cn: 孩子闻到变质食物时捏住鼻子

branches.en: a runner flat on the ice after a bad landing
branches.cn: 跑步的人重重摔在冰面上

branches.en: a storm tearing at the roof of a coastal house
branches.cn: 风暴撕扯海边房屋的屋顶

branches.en: a whispered rumour passing from desk to desk
branches.cn: 一句悄悄话从一张桌子传到另一张桌子

intro.en: The word has a disputed stem and three productive English endings, which build the adjective, the noun and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词有一个来源有争议的词干和三个能产的英语词尾，分别构成形容词、名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate has been recorded for this word; the early source itself is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，其早期来源本身也不确定。

items.meaning: forming adjectives from nouns or stems

definition_zh: 民族；国家；全体国民；（历史用法）部落、族群
definition_en: a people who share a common origin, history or identity, especially when organized as a state
core_image: 一条手绘的边界线穿过同一片口音相同的村庄，把同一个集市分成两半
scene: 旧地图铺在桌上，一条边界线正好穿过说同一种口音的几个村庄，教书的人用手指顺着线划过。The nation was divided by a border drawn through its villages.
sceneCN: 这里 nation 指「共享同一种身份与语言的一群人」（第 2 个义项：以共同出身、语言或历史凝聚的群体，未必与国家疆界重合）；句意为这个民族被一条穿过其村庄的边界分成了两半。图中可辨识物件：旧地图、铅笔画的边界、被切开的集市、手指；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 民族；国家；全体国民（可数，复数 nations）

collocations.zh: 一个由移民构成的国家

derivatives.zh: 国家的；民族的（nation 加 -al，指属于整个民族的）
国籍；民族（national 加 -ity，指法律或族群身份）
民族主义（national 加 -ism，指以民族为中心的主张）
民族主义者；民族主义的（national 加 -ist）
收归国有；使全国化（national 加 -ize，使转为国家所有）
出生；诞生（拉丁 nasci 加 -ity，与 nation 同出「出生」词根）
本地的；本地人（拉丁 nativus，同出 nasci「出生」）

senses.title: A sovereign country
senses.definition: an independent state with its own government, territory and seat at international bodies
senses.definitionCN: 拥有自己的政府、领土与国际组织席位的独立国家
senses.example: The two nations opened embassies within a year of the ceasefire.
senses.exampleCN: 停火一年之内，这两个国家互设了大使馆。
senses.why: Because a people organized as a state is the modern default, the plain everyday sense of the word is simply 'country'.
senses.whyCN: 因为「组织成国家的一群人」是现代默认形态，所以这个词最日常的意思就是「国家」。

senses.title: A people sharing identity
senses.definition: a group held together by a common language, history or sense of belonging, whether or not it has a state
senses.definitionCN: 由共同语言、历史或归属感凝聚的群体，无论是否拥有国家
senses.example: The nation was divided by a border drawn through its villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个民族被一条穿过其村庄的边界分成了两半。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a people born together, and that sense survives precisely where the state and the people do not match.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「同出一源的一群人」，这一意思恰恰在国家与人群不重合之处延续下来。

senses.title: The citizenry taken as one body
senses.definition: the whole body of citizens, often addressed as a single moral actor in speeches
senses.definitionCN: 全体公民的整体，常在演说中被当作单一的道义行动者来称呼
senses.example: The nation was asked to give up one holiday to fund the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 全体国民被要求放弃一个假日，为医院筹资。
senses.why: Once everyone is imagined as one body, speakers can address the whole population as a single person who decides.
senses.whyCN: 一旦所有人被想象成一个整体，演说者就能把全体人口当作一个做决定的单数人格来称呼。

senses.title: A tribe or ethnic people in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中的部落或族群
senses.definition: a people or tribe described in history and anthropology, as in the nations of the ancient Near East
senses.definitionCN: 历史学与人类学中描述的族群或部落，如古代近东诸族
senses.example: The chronicle lists the nations that sent tribute to the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这部编年史列出了向都城进贡的各族。
senses.why: Natio in Latin could mean any group of common birth, and that broad sense passed into older English historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 natio 可指任何同出一源的群体，这一宽泛含义进入了较早的英语历史写作。

senses.title: A formally recognized tribal nation
senses.titleCN: 获正式承认的原住民族
senses.definition: the official self-designation of many Native American peoples, as in the Navajo Nation
senses.definitionCN: 许多北美原住民族群的正式自称，如纳瓦霍族
senses.example: The tribal council speaks for the nation in negotiations with the federal government.
senses.exampleCN: 部落议会在与联邦政府的谈判中代表该民族发言。
senses.why: Sovereignty language was borrowed from international law, so tribes adopted 'nation' to assert a political status older than the state.
senses.whyCN: 主权话语借自国际法，因此各部落采用「nation」来主张一种比国家更古老的政治地位。

senses.title: The community of states
senses.titleCN: 国际社会中的国家共同体
senses.definition: the collectivity of states acting together, as in 'the community of nations' or 'the family of nations'
senses.definitionCN: 共同行动的各国整体，如「国际社会」「国家大家庭」
senses.example: The community of nations voted to send observers.
senses.exampleCN: 国际社会投票决定派出观察员。
senses.why: When states are treated as persons in international law, their society is naturally described as a group of nations.
senses.whyCN: 当国家在国际法中被当作人格，它们的共同体自然就被描述为一群国家。

senses.title: A student nation at older universities
senses.titleCN: 旧式大学中的学生同乡会
senses.definition: a regional association of students at historic Scandinavian and other European universities
senses.definitionCN: 北欧及欧洲其他历史悠久的大学中，按地区组成的学生团体
senses.example: He joined the northern nation and ate at its hall every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他加入了北方学生同乡会，每晚都在其食堂吃饭。
senses.why: The word once meant simply a group of people of common origin, which is exactly what a regional student society is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾经只表示同出一源的一群人，而按地区组成的学生团体正是如此。

senses.title: A rhetorical collective of like-minded people
senses.titleCN: 修辞上指志趣相同的一群人
senses.definition: a figurative use such as 'a nation of readers' or 'a nation of shopkeepers', naming a large group by its shared habit
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，如「阅读的民族」「店主的国家」，以共同习惯命名一大群人
senses.example: The magazine called its subscribers a nation of careful readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志把它的订户称为一个认真阅读的民族。
senses.why: The rhetorical force comes from treating a shared practice as a common birth, which is the word's original image.

intro.en: Nation comes from a Latin noun of birth, narrowed in French toward a political people and then widened again in English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nation 来自一个表示出生的拉丁名词，在法语中被收窄为政治意义上的国民，进入英语后又重新变宽。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nasci 'to be born' is generally thought to descend from a root meaning 'to beget', the same stock as gignere 'to produce' and genus 'race, kind'.
items.cn: nasci「出生」一般认为源自表示「生育」的词根，与 gignere「产生」、genus「种族、种类」同族。

items.en: Natio first named a birth or an origin, then a body of people of common birth; Roman writers also used it for foreigners living in one quarter of the city.
items.cn: natio 最初指出生或出身，继而指同出一源的一群人；罗马作家也用它指聚居城中一区的异邦人。

items.en: Old French nation narrowed the word to a political people or a province, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 nation 把词义收窄为政治意义上的国民或一个行省，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: English first used the word for a people of common stock, then for the whole political community of a kingdom, then for a sovereign state.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指同出一源的族群，继而指一个王国中的整体政治共同体，再指主权国家。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the word was joined to -state and -hood, and the pairing of nation and state became the normal form of political organization.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪，这个词与 state、hood 组合，民族与国家的配对成为常见的政治组织形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (dates and reconstruction): the exact point at which the word shifted from a birth-group to a sovereign state is not recorded, and the pre-Latin root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（年代与重构）：从出生群体转向主权国家的确切时点没有记载；拉丁语之前的词根形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the birth root and are constantly confused; group two holds words for the same large entity seen from different angles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「出生」词根、极易混淆的词；第二组是从不同角度指同一大实体的词。

entries.definition: The status of belonging to a state in law, or to an ethnic group; it names a status, while nation names the group itself.

normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「一同出生的一群人」走到一种法律身份，几个词尾标记了这段路程。

normal.en: Nation and nationality share the Latin stem nat-, born, so the word is about where a person comes from.
normal.cn: nation 与 nationality 共用拉丁词干 nat-（出生），所以这个词说的是人从哪里来。

normal.en: National adds -al to nation; nationality adds -ity to national, turning a description into a status.
normal.cn: national 在 nation 后加 -al；nationality 在 national 后加 -ity，把描述变成一种身份。

normal.en: Dual nationality is a fixed phrase, and the adjective dual never changes with the noun.
normal.cn: dual nationality 是固定搭配，dual 这个形容词不随名词变化。

normal.en: Minority nationality is the usual phrase in Chinese English for an ethnic group smaller than the majority.
normal.cn: minority nationality 是中国英语里指少数族群常用的说法。

normal.en: Citizenship is the everyday word for rights, nationality the legal and formal word for status.
normal.cn: citizenship 是讲权利的日常说法，nationality 是讲身份的法律正式说法。

abstract.en: A word built on birth reminds us that a passport is a piece of paper laid over the fact of where someone was born.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「出生」之上的词提醒人：护照只是盖在「人在何处出生」这个事实之上的一张纸。

abstract.en: Nationality can be one person's paper and a whole people's name at the same time, which is why it feels both personal and political.
abstract.cn: nationality 既可以是某人的一张纸，也可以是一整群人的名字，所以它既私人又政治。

abstract.en: When the same word covers a passport and a people, identity is being asked to carry two very different weights.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指护照又指民族，说明身份这个概念被迫承担两种很不同的重量。

examples.en: She has dual nationality.
examples.cn: 她拥有双重国籍。

examples.en: People of many nationalities live in the capital.
examples.cn: 首都居住着许多不同民族的人。

examples.en: The law grants nationality to children born here.
examples.cn: 法律赋予在此出生的孩子国籍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拿新人来提」——递上材料换本新护照，记住 nationality 是国籍。

root: 拉丁语 nasci（出生）→ natio（一同出生的人群、民族）→ 古法语 nacion → 英语 nationality（十七世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a group born together; from it the word divides into legal nationality, ethnic group and the people as a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一同出生的一群人；由此分出法律上的国籍、民族群体以及作为整体的国民。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark passport opening to show a crest and a face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本深色护照翻开，露出国徽与持照人的脸。

branches.cn: 一枚印章落在新护照的第一页

branches.cn: 旅客排成长队，手里拿着不同颜色的护照

branches.cn: 一个集市上同时有人讲几种语言的村庄

branches.cn: 汇聚许多族群服饰的节日

branches.cn: 广场上整片人群齐唱一首国歌

definition_zh: 自然的；天然的；天生的；正常的
definition_en: existing in nature rather than made by people; also inborn, and normal or expected
core_image: 一株野草从石缝里自己钻出来，没有人去栽种
scene: 山脚下有一片从未开垦的林地，藤蔓顺着倒下的树干自己爬上去。The reserve protects the natural habitat of the local birds.
sceneCN: 这里 natural 是「自然的、天然的」（第 1 个义项：非人造）；句意为保护区守护当地鸟类的天然栖息地。图中可辨识物件：倒木、藤蔓、林地。

pos.zh: 自然的；天然的；天生的；正常的

由 natural 加 -ness 构成，义为「自然；不做作」
