senses.title: Existing in nature, not made by people
senses.definition: found in nature and produced without human making or control
senses.definitionCN: 存在于自然界、并非由人制造或控制而产生的
senses.example: The park protects the natural habitat of the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园保护着鸟类的天然栖息地。
senses.why: The Latin noun natura names the way things are born and grow, so natural starts from what comes into being without human hands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 natura 指事物出生、生长的样子，所以 natural 的起点是未经人手而生成的东西。

senses.title: Inborn rather than learned
senses.definition: present in a person or animal from birth and not learned
senses.definitionCN: 人与生俱来、并非后天学到的
senses.example: She has a natural gift for languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生就有语言天赋。
senses.why: If natura is the way something is born, a quality that arrives at birth is literally natural, which is why talent can be natural.
senses.whyCN: 既然 natura 指事物出生时的样子，出生就带来的特质自然就是「天生的」，天赋也就能说成 natural。

senses.title: Normal and to be expected
senses.definition: what normally happens and therefore does not surprise anyone
senses.definitionCN: 按常理会发生，因此不令人意外
senses.example: It is natural to feel nervous before a test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前感到紧张是正常的。
senses.why: What follows nature follows a regular course, so natural extends from how things grow to how things usually happen.
senses.whyCN: 顺着本性发展的东西有其常规，于是 natural 从「事物如何生长」扩展到「事情通常如何发生」。

senses.title: Relaxed and not put on
senses.definition: used of behaviour or manner that is easy and sincere, with no pretending
senses.definitionCN: 形容举止轻松真诚，不装样子
senses.example: His smile was warm and natural.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑容温暖而自然。
senses.why: A person who behaves as nature made them, without forcing a pose, looks natural, which gives the word its social sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个人按本性行事、不硬摆姿势，看上去就是 natural，这就是这个词的社交义。

intro.en: Natural comes from the Latin noun natura, which itself grows out of nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: natural 来自拉丁名词 natura，而 natura 又由 nasci（出生）生长出来。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born, the root behind nature, native and innate.
items.cn: nasci 意为出生，是 nature、native、innate 共同的根。

items.en: Natura named the character or course of things, what a thing is born to be.
items.cn: natura 指事物的本性或进程，即事物生来就该有的样子。

items.en: Naturalis meant belonging to nature or coming from birth.
items.cn: naturalis 意为属于自然的，或与生俱来的。

items.en: Old French naturel passed into Middle English natural, keeping both the world sense and the inborn sense.
items.cn: 古法语 naturel 进入中古英语作 natural，同时保留「自然界」和「天生」两义。

items.en: Modern English adds the meanings normal and unaffected, which grow from the idea of following nature.
items.cn: 现代英语又添「正常」与「不做作」两义，都由「顺其自然」的想法长出。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same birth stem; the near-meaning group collects words for what is normal and inborn.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「出生」词干上的词；近义组收表示正常与天生的词。

entries.definition: The physical world and the character built into a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 物质世界，以及事物内在的本性。

entries.definition: Born in a particular place, or belonging there by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 在某个地方出生的；原产的。

entries.definition: Present in a person from birth, not learned.
entries.definitionCN: 人与生俱来的，并非学来的。

entries.definition: What is usual and expected, with nothing odd about it.
entries.definitionCN: 通常而合乎预期的，没有异常之处。

entries.definition: Existing in a person from birth rather than gained later.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来而非后天获得的。

entries.definition: Grown or produced without artificial chemicals or processes.
entries.definitionCN: 不使用人工化学物或工艺而生长、生产的。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun of birth and three English endings that build an adverb, a noun and a verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由一个表示「出生」的拉丁名词和三个英语词尾支撑，分别构成副词、名词和动词。

normal.en: Natura is Latin for the way things are born and grow, so natural is first about the world, not about people.
normal.cn: natura 是拉丁语中事物出生、生长的样子，所以 natural 首先说的是世界，而不是人。

normal.en: Naturally adds -ly, and it doubles as an answer word meaning of course.
normal.cn: naturally 加 -ly 构成，它还有一个「当然」的用法。

normal.en: Native and innate share the same birth root, one meaning born in a place, the other born in a person.
normal.cn: native 与 innate 共用同一个「出生」的词根，一个指在某地出生，一个指天生。

normal.en: Natural gas and natural resources are fixed phrases, so natural here means unprocessed, not easy.
normal.cn: natural gas 与 natural resources 是固定搭配，这里的 natural 指未经加工，而不是轻松。

normal.en: A natural death means death by age or illness, not by accident or violence.
normal.cn: natural death 指因年老或疾病死亡，而不是意外或暴力致死。

abstract.en: A word that begins with the world and ends with good manners shows how deeply English ties sincerity to nature.
abstract.cn: 一个词从自然界开始、到得体举止结束，说明英语把「真诚」紧紧系在「自然」上。

abstract.en: Calling something natural is often a quiet claim that nothing has been added to it.
abstract.cn: 说某物是 natural，常常是在悄悄声明没有往里面添加别的东西。

abstract.en: When a gift is called natural, praise and modesty arrive in the same word.
abstract.cn: 当一份天赋被叫作 natural，赞美与谦逊同时落在同一个词里。

examples.en: This valley is one of the few natural habitats left for the species.
examples.cn: 这条山谷是该物种仅存的几处天然栖息地之一。

examples.en: He has a natural ability to make strangers feel at ease.
examples.cn: 他天生就有让陌生人放松的本事。

examples.en: It is natural to miss home during the first month abroad.
examples.cn: 出国头一个月想家是正常的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈求若」——真正的自然不必强求，顺其自然就会来；记住 natural 是自然的。

root: 拉丁语 nasci（出生）→ natura（本性、自然）→ naturalis（属于自然的）→ 古法语 naturel → 中古英语 natural。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is what nature produces; from it the word reaches inborn qualities, expected behaviour and social ease.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是自然界生成的东西；由此延伸到天生的特质、合乎常理的行为以及举止自然。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wild shoot pushing out of a crack in the rock, planted by nobody.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株野草从石缝里自己钻出来，没有人去栽种。

branches.en: a forest floor left alone for a hundred years
branches.cn: 一百年没人打扰的林地

branches.en: a singer whose voice seems to need no training
branches.cn: 嗓音仿佛无需训练的歌者

branches.en: a child who can draw before anyone teaches her
branches.cn: 还没人教就会画画的女孩

branches.en: guests arriving late after a storm
branches.cn: 暴风雨后迟到的客人

branches.en: a host laughing without planning the joke
branches.cn: 没准备笑话却笑出声的主人

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin stem for birth, the noun for nature, and three English endings that widen it into a family.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「出生」的拉丁词干、表示自然的名词，以及三个扩大词族的英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 自然地；天生地；理所当然地；未经人工干预地；不做作地
definition_en: in a natural way, by nature, or as one would reasonably expect
core_image: 一粒种子落在土里，没有支架，也没有指令，它自己朝光长出一片叶子。
scene: 朋友听说你刚搬到海边，笑着说，这大概会自然而然发生。Living by the sea, you will naturally start swimming every day.
sceneCN: 这里 naturally 是“理所当然地、自然而然”（第 3 个义项）；句意：住在海边，你自然会开始每天游泳；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 自然地；天生地；理所当然地；未经人工干预地；不做作地

collocations.zh: 生来就会；做起来很自然

derivatives.zh: 自然；天性；本质
自然的；天生的；正常的
自然；不做作
使归化；使自然化

senses.title: In nature's own way
senses.titleCN: 以自然的方式：不按人为规矩来
senses.definition: in a way that follows nature rather than human design or convention
senses.definitionCN: 依照自然而非人为设计或惯例的方式进行
senses.example: The river runs naturally through the valley, without any concrete banks.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河自然地流过山谷，两岸没有水泥护岸。
senses.why: The adverb describes the manner of an action: it happens as nature would have it, so the absence of human arrangement is the point.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词描述动作的方式：事情按自然本来的样子发生，所以“没有人为安排”正是重点。

senses.title: From birth, by temperament
senses.titleCN: 天生地：生来就带着的本事或性情
senses.definition: as a result of inborn ability or character rather than training
senses.definitionCN: 出于与生俱来的能力或性格，而非后天训练
senses.example: She naturally remembers faces, even ones she has seen only once.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生记得住面孔，哪怕只见过一次。
senses.why: Here the adverb points to the origin of an ability: the talent is treated as part of the person's constitution, not as an acquired skill.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词指向能力的来源：这份才能被视为个人禀赋的一部分，而不是后天习得的技能。

senses.title: As you would expect
senses.titleCN: 理所当然：事情本就该这样
senses.definition: as is reasonable or unsurprising, given the circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 在那种情形下合乎情理、并不令人意外
senses.example: Naturally, the children were excited the night before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前一晚孩子们很兴奋，这是理所当然的。
senses.why: This sense is about inference, not nature: the speaker says the outcome follows so obviously that no explanation is needed.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项关乎推理而非自然：说话者表示结果显然如此，根本无须解释。

senses.title: Without human help
senses.titleCN: 未经人工干预：自己长出来的
senses.definition: happening or existing without cultivation, manufacture, or intervention
senses.definitionCN: 在没有栽培、制造或人为干预的情况下发生或存在
senses.example: The valley is naturally protected from strong winds by its surrounding hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷因四周的丘陵而天然不受强风侵袭。
senses.why: The word marks a cause that is not human: whatever produced the result was already there, so no one deserves credit or blame for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出非人为的原因：产生结果的东西本来就存在，因此无人该为此受功或受责。

senses.title: Without pretending
senses.titleCN: 不做作：不摆姿态、不加表演
senses.definition: in a relaxed and sincere manner that shows no affectation
senses.definitionCN: 以放松而真诚的方式，不显出做作
senses.example: On camera she laughed naturally, not the way she laughed in advertisements.
senses.exampleCN: 镜头前她笑得很自然，不是广告里那种笑法。
senses.why: Praise of natural behaviour measures the distance between a person and a performance; the smaller the distance, the more naturally it is done.
senses.whyCN: 称赞举止自然，衡量的是“人”与“表演”之间的距离；距离越小，就做得越自然。

senses.title: By logical consequence
senses.titleCN: 顺理成章：顺着前提必然走到这里
senses.definition: as a necessary or logical consequence of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 作为先前事情必然或合乎逻辑的结果
senses.example: Naturally, a longer delay meant a higher final cost.
senses.exampleCN: 工期拖得更久，最终成本自然更高。
senses.why: The sense borrows the idea of nature as an inevitable order and applies it to reasoning: given the premise, the conclusion could hardly be otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项借用了“自然是一种必然秩序”的观念，并把它用于推理：前提既定，结论几乎不可能不是这样。

senses.title: Found in the wild
senses.titleCN: 天然存在：自然界里本来就有
senses.definition: occurring in nature rather than being made or introduced by people
senses.definitionCN: 存在于自然界，而非由人制造或引入
senses.example: The element is naturally present in seawater at a very low concentration.
senses.exampleCN: 这种元素天然存在于海水中，浓度极低。
senses.why: In science the word distinguishes a substance that was already in the environment from one released or synthesised by humans.
senses.whyCN: 在科学语境里，这个词区分“本来就在环境中的物质”与“人类释放或合成的物质”。

senses.title: Easily and smoothly
senses.titleCN: 从容自如：做起来不费劲
senses.definition: with ease and fluency, as if no effort were required
senses.definitionCN: 轻松流畅地，仿佛不需要用力
senses.example: After a month of practice, the steps came naturally to him.
senses.exampleCN: 练了一个月后，这些步骤他做起来已从容自如。
senses.why: Skill that has become second nature no longer shows the seams of conscious control; the adverb reports that ease rather than describing the world.
senses.whyCN: 熟练到成为第二天性时，动作不再露出刻意控制的痕迹；这个副词报告的是这种轻松，而不是在描述世界。

intro.en: Naturally is natural plus the adverb suffix -ly. Natural goes back through French to Latin natura and the verb nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: naturally 是 natural 加副词后缀 -ly。natural 经法语上溯至拉丁语 natura 与动词 nasci“出生”。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born or to arise. From it came natura, the condition and character one has at birth.
items.cn: nasci 意为“出生、产生”。由它派生出 natura，指出生时的状况与禀性。

items.en: Naturalis described what belongs to nature or comes from it, as opposed to what art or human skill produces.
items.cn: naturalis 描述属于自然或来自自然的东西，与技艺或人力所产相对。

items.en: Old French naturel kept both senses: the physical world and a person's inborn disposition.
items.cn: 古法语 naturel 保留两层含义：物质世界，以及人的固有性情。

items.en: English formed adverbs with -ly from Old English -lice. Naturally therefore means 'in a natural manner' before it means 'of course'.
items.cn: 英语用 -ly（古英语 -lice）构成副词。因此 naturally 先表示“以自然的方式”，之后才引申出“当然”。

items.en: The 'as expected' sense grew out of the idea that nature follows a fixed order: what is natural is also what regularly happens.
items.cn: “如所预料”义由“自然遵循固定秩序”的观念生长出来：合乎自然的，也就是经常发生的。

items.en: Science writing added naturally occurring; speech and performance writing added the sense of ease without affectation.
items.cn: 科学写作发展出 naturally occurring（天然存在）；言语与表演领域则发展出“从容不做作”的义项。

note.en: The first group shares the nature root; the second compares adverbs that describe how an action comes about.
note.cn: 第一组共享 nature 词根；第二组比较几个描述“动作如何发生”的副词。

entries.definition: existing in nature, inborn, or normal. It modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 自然界存在的、天生的或正常的；修饰名词。

entries.definition: the physical world, or the essential character of something.
entries.definitionCN: 物质世界，或某物的本质特性。

entries.definition: the quality of being natural or free from affectation.
entries.definitionCN: 自然、不做作的性质。

entries.definition: as everyone knows or expects. It marks the obviousness of a fact, not its origin.
entries.definitionCN: 众所周知或如人所料；标出事实的显然，而不涉其来源。

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be avoided. It is stronger than naturally and implies necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 以无法避免的方式；比 naturally 更强，含必然性。

entries.definition: by automatic animal impulse rather than thought. It applies to living creatures.
entries.definitionCN: 凭本能的自动冲动而非思考；适用于生物。

entries.definition: from one's own impulse, without planning; also happening without external cause.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自身冲动、未经计划；也指无外在原因地发生。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: natural + -ly. The suffix simply turns the adjective into an adverb, so the meaning tracks natural.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：natural 加 -ly。后缀只是把形容词变成副词，词义随 natural 走。

normal.en: Natural + -ly: do it the way nature would, with no scaffolding.
normal.cn: natural 加 -ly：照自然的方式做，不加支架。

normal.en: A talent you never trained comes naturally; a habit you drilled also comes naturally after enough practice.
normal.cn: 没练过的才能，说起来就是“生来就会”；练够了的习惯，用起来也同样轻松自如。

normal.en: In a chemistry paper, naturally means it was already in the water.
normal.cn: 在化学论文里，naturally 表示它本来就在水里。

normal.en: Naturally at the start of a sentence usually means 'as you can guess'.
normal.cn: naturally 放在句首，通常就是“你猜也猜得到”。

normal.en: A good actor makes a rehearsed line sound naturally spoken.
normal.cn: 好演员能把排练过的台词说得像自然说出的一样。

abstract.en: Nature and reason share one adverb: what always happens and what must follow are felt to be the same order.
abstract.cn: 自然与理性共用一个副词：总会发生的事与必然推出的事，被感受为同一种秩序。

abstract.en: Saying 'naturally' hides who arranged the conditions; it presents a result as if no one had chosen it.
abstract.cn: 说 naturally 会隐藏是谁安排了条件：它把结果呈现得好像无人选择过。

abstract.en: Effortless skill is nature edited by years of practice, and the adverb keeps the editing out of sight.
abstract.cn: 举重若轻的技艺，是被多年练习剪辑过的自然；而这个副词把剪辑痕迹藏在镜头外。

examples.en: The lake is naturally too cold for swimming until late June.
examples.cn: 这个湖天然太冷，要到六月下旬才适合游泳。

examples.en: Naturally, the students who read the whole book did better on the essay question.
examples.cn: 读过整本书的学生在论述题上表现更好，这是理所当然的。

examples.en: She stepped onto the stage and began to speak naturally, as if the audience were old friends.
examples.cn: 她走上台，自然地开口，仿佛观众都是老朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: natural（自然的）+ ly（地）——自然地；事情按常理发展，也就成了“当然”。

root: 由 natural（自然的，源自拉丁语 natura“出生、本性”，出自 nasci“出生”）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，本义为“以自然的方式”，后引申为“天生地、理所当然地”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of naturally. One thread runs through them: something happens without visible human arrangement. That can mean without cultivation, without training, without affectation, or simply without any need to explain.
sensesIntro.cn: naturally 的八个义项由一条线串起：事情发生，却看不出人为安排。这可以指未经栽培、未经训练、不加做作，或干脆无须解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed in bare soil, growing toward the light with no stake and no instruction.
core.cn: 核心意象：裸土里的一粒种子，没有支架也没有指令，自己朝光生长。

branches.en: WITHOUT HUMAN DESIGN: a free river and an element already in seawater both exist before anyone acts.
branches.cn: 无人为设计：自由流淌的河与海水中本就存在的元素，都在人行动之前就已存在。

branches.en: WITHOUT TRAINING: inborn memory and practised ease both look as if no learning took place.
branches.cn: 未经训练：天生的记忆力与练成的从容，看起来都像没有学习过。

branches.en: WITHOUT EXPLANATION: 'as you would expect' and 'by consequence' both present the result as obvious.
branches.cn: 无须解释：“如你所料”与“顺理成章”都把结果呈现为显然。

branches.en: WITHOUT CULTIVATION: shelter and protection supplied by terrain rather than by builders.
branches.cn: 未经栽培：由地形而非建造者提供的遮蔽与保护。

branches.en: WITHOUT PERFORMANCE: behaviour that does not advertise itself as behaviour.
branches.cn: 不加表演：举止不把自己标榜为“举止”。

intro.en: Naturally is natural plus -ly, the standard English adverb suffix. The family spreads through -ness, -ism, -ist, -ize, and the prefix un-.
intro.cn: naturally 是 natural 加 -ly，即英语标准副词后缀。词族再通过 -ness、-ism、-ist、-ize 与否定前缀 un- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is nasci, to be born, giving natura and naturalis. English -ly descends from Old English -lice, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 nasci“出生”，由此得到 natura 与 naturalis。英语 -ly 则源自古英语 -lice，并非来自拉丁语。

items.meaning: the physical world, or the inborn character of something
items.meaningCN: 自然界；或事物的固有本性
items.example: The nature of the clay decides how the pot will fire.
items.exampleCN: 陶土的性质决定这只陶罐烧成后的样子。

items.meaning: existing in nature, inborn, or normal
items.meaningCN: 自然存在的；天生的；正常的
items.example: The harbour is a natural shelter for small boats.
items.exampleCN: 这个港湾是小船天然的避风处。

items.meaning: in a natural manner; as expected
items.meaningCN: 以自然的方式；如所预料
items.example: The trail climbs naturally along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 这条小径顺着山脊自然向上延伸。

items.meaning: the quality of being natural or unaffected
items.example: The naturalness of her voice made the recording easy to trust.
items.exampleCN: 她声音里的自然感让这段录音容易让人信服。

items.meaning: the view that nature is all of reality
items.meaningCN: 自然即全部现实的学说
items.example: Naturalism rejects explanations that step outside nature.
items.exampleCN: 自然主义拒绝越出自然之外的解释。

items.meaning: a field researcher of living things
items.meaningCN: 野外研究生物的人；博物学家
items.example: The naturalist noted the first migrants of spring.
items.exampleCN: 这位博物学家记下了春天第一批迁徙的鸟。

items.meaning: to make natural, or to establish a species or word as native
items.meaningCN: 使自然化；使物种或词语归化
items.example: The plant naturalized quickly in the wet soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种植物在湿土中很快归化了。

items.meaning: contrary to nature or to normal feeling
items.example: The brightness of the sky at midnight seemed unnatural.
items.exampleCN: 午夜天空的亮度显得反常。

items.meaningCN: 存在于自然秩序之外的；超自然的
items.example: The story adds a supernatural explanation to a real famine.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事给一场真实的饥荒加上了超自然解释。

definition_zh: 海军的；军舰的；海战的
definition_en: belonging to a navy or its warships, or connected with war at sea
core_image: 灰色军舰的舰首切开浪头，甲板上一排水兵抬手敬礼
scene: 港口外的海面灰蒙蒙的，一排军舰挂着旗，贴着水线缓缓出港。A naval exercise was held off the coast last month.
sceneCN: 这里 naval 是「海军的」（第 1 个义项：属于海军）；句意为上个月在近海举行了一场海军演习。图中可辨识物件：军舰、舰旗、海面。

derivatives.zh: 与 naval 同出拉丁语 navis（船）的同源词，义为「海军；舰队」
同出 navis（船），由 navis 与 agere（驾驶）合成，义为「航行；导航」
由 navigate 加 -ion 构成，义为「航行；航海术」

senses.title: Belonging to a navy
senses.definition: connected with a country's navy, the branch of its armed forces that fights at sea
senses.definitionCN: 与一个国家的海军相关，即其武装力量中在海上作战的军种
senses.example: The country expanded its naval forces last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家去年扩充了海军部队。
senses.why: The Latin adjective navalis meant of ships, and since a fleet is made of ships, the word naturally names the service that operates them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词 navalis 意为「船的」，而舰队由船组成，这个词自然就用来指操纵船舰的军种。

senses.title: Of warships and their equipment
senses.definition: used of ships built for war and the bases, yards or equipment that serve them
senses.definitionCN: 用于为作战建造的舰船，以及为其服务的基地、船厂或装备
senses.example: The yard repairs naval vessels from several countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家船厂修理来自几个国家的海军舰艇。
senses.why: If navalis belongs to ships, it can describe the ships themselves, so a naval vessel is simply a ship built for war.
senses.whyCN: 既然 navalis 属于船，它也能形容船本身，所以 naval vessel 就是为战争建造的舰船。

senses.title: Connected with war at sea
senses.definition: describing battles, strategy or power exercised at sea rather than on land
senses.definitionCN: 描述在海上而非陆地上进行的战斗、战略或力量
senses.example: The two powers fought a naval battle in the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在海峡打了一场海战。
senses.why: From ships and their crews the word extends to the fighting itself, so any clash decided by fleets is naval.
senses.whyCN: 词义从船舰与舰员延伸到作战本身，所以由舰队决定胜负的交锋都叫 naval。

intro.en: Naval descends from the Latin word for ship, and it keeps that narrow maritime meaning in modern English.
intro.cn: naval 源自拉丁语中表示「船」的词，并在现代英语里保留了这个狭窄的海上含义。

items.en: Navis was the ordinary Latin word for a ship, and it stands behind navy, navigate and naval.
items.cn: navis 是拉丁语里普通的「船」字，是 navy、navigate、naval 共同的源头。

items.en: The adjective navalis meant of a ship or of ships, and it was used of fleets and sea forces.
items.cn: 形容词 navalis 意为「船的」，用于舰队和海上力量。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective as naval, keeping the sense of ships and the sea.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 naval，保留船与海的含义。

items.en: Middle English used naval for things belonging to ships, especially warships.
items.cn: 中古英语用 naval 指属于船的事物，尤指战舰。

items.en: Modern English limits naval to the navy and sea warfare, while navy names the force itself.
items.cn: 现代英语把 naval 限定在海军与海战，而 navy 指这支力量本身。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for ship, its adjective, and English words that keep the same maritime root.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示「船」的名词、它的形容词，以及共享同一海上词根的英语词共同支撑。

normal.en: Navis is Latin for ship, so every word in this family keeps a trace of a hull on water.
normal.cn: navis 是拉丁语的「船」，这一族词都留着水面上船身的影子。

normal.en: Navy is the force, naval is the adjective that describes it, just as army and military divide the work.
normal.cn: navy 是这支力量，naval 是描述它的形容词，就像 army 与 military 的分工。

normal.en: Navigate joins navis with agere, to drive, so it literally means to drive a ship.
normal.cn: navigate 把 navis 与 agere（驾驶）合起来，字面就是「驾驶船」。

normal.en: Navel sounds the same as naval but belongs to a Germanic root for the belly, so keep the two apart.
normal.cn: navel 与 naval 读音相同，却来自表示腹部的日耳曼词根，要把两个词分开。

normal.en: Naval battle, naval base and naval officer all fix the word to the sea service, not to ships in general.
normal.cn: naval battle、naval base 与 naval officer 都把词固定在海上军种，而不是泛指船。

abstract.en: A word for ship is also the word for a nation's reach across water: the hull becomes a border.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「船」的词也成了国家跨海而去的触角：船身变成了边界。

abstract.en: Naval power is measured less by ships than by the sea lanes a fleet can keep open.
abstract.cn: 衡量海上力量，与其说看舰船数量，不如说看一支舰队能守住多少航道。

abstract.en: Keeping naval and navel apart is a small reminder that sound and sense travel on different roads.
abstract.cn: 把 naval 与 navel 分开，是一个小提醒：读音与意义走的是不同的路。

examples.en: The fleet won a decisive naval battle in the strait.
examples.cn: 舰队在海峡赢得了一场决定性的海战。

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin noun for ship, its adjective form and an English adjective ending, with related words that keep the same root.
